item.title: Bruins’ Mittelstadt Embracing, Thriving in Shutdown Role
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Boston Bruins have tasked Casey Mittelstadt with shutting down opposing stars, but that has not stopped him from putting up some of the best offensive numbers of his career. Through the first 20 games of the season, Mittelstadt is tied for second on the team with seven goals. He’s shooting at a 24.1% rate, which shatters the previous career high he set last season (18.8%). He has 12 points this season, and his plus-11 rating is second on the team to Will Borgen . For the second straight year, Mittelstadt is on the Bruins’ shutdown forward line. He is the only one from last year’s second line to remain in that role this season. He’s been joined on the third line by Elias Lindholm , James Hagens , and, more recently with Hagens’ injury , Marat Khusnutdinov . “You could tell right away [he had] a really good jump. I feel like he feels very comfortable in that role, too,” Marco Sturm said of Mittelstadt on Saturday. “I think that changed since I put him in a checking line and a shutdown line role. And I think he likes that, because he always knows when he takes care of his own end, he’s going to get some really good opportunities. And right now, he’s been around the net too.” With Mittelstadt on the ice this season at 5-on-5, the Bruins have outscored their opponents 17-6 . They also hold a commanding 10-2 advantage in high-danger goals, showing they have been both effective at limiting opponents and capitalizing on their own chances. Marco Sturm has routinely tasked Mittelstadt’s line with the opposition’s top line. The trio has kept Macklin Celebrini , Jack Eichel , and Sidney Crosby off the scoresheet at 5-on-5 this season, all while generating offense of their own. The Bruins also have a 59.32% share of expected goals with Mittelstadt on the ice, which soars above his career-high number of 51.53% in 2023-24. “We always said, with so much skill, he should be the goal scorer. He still is, but he’s just in a different role,” Sturm said. “For me, he’s way more comfortable now, and he likes those challenges, and they want to be out there against the best.” Casey Mittelstadt on matching up against the Celebrini line:⁰ “I mean, obviously, he’s a heck of a player. I think we all know that, and he has good players around him as well, but I think a lot of that credit goes to Lindy (Elias).” “Lindy does a heck of a job in all three… pic.twitter.com/DVCH472ylY — Jack Studley (@jackstudley13) October 25, 2026 While Mittelstadt has been quick to credit his linemates, Sturm also pointed to the work he put in over the summer as a reason for his success. “A little bit of a combination. You know, the consistency of the coaching staff and being here for a while has really benefited me well.” Mittelstadt’s strong start also comes in the final year of his three-year deal, which carries a $5.75 million cap hit. He is scheduled to become an unrestricted free agent for the first time in his career this summer. AFP Analytics projects him to sign a four-year deal with a $6.8 million cap hit. item.title: Collinsworth slams Jordan Battle for Bengals-Steelers taunting penalty
item.description: NBC Sports analyst and former Cincinnati Bengals receiver Cris Collinsworth blasted defensive back Jordan Battle for his taunting penalty during the second quarter of the NFL Week 10 game between the Bengals and the Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium on NBC's Sunday Night Football . Battle stood over Steelers receiver DK Metcalf after breaking up an Aaron Rodgers pass to Metcalf. "He just sat there and looked at him and cost his team 15 yards, and gave the Steelers a chance to wake up," Collinsworth said of Battle's penalty during the broadcast. Battle was limited during the week before the Bengals' Week 9 win against Atlanta in Spain because of a hamstring injury. The NFL announced a fine of $21,623 for Battle for unnecessary roughness (use of the helmet) during the Bengals' Week 5 win in Miami . Battle was limited during the week before the Bengals' loss to Jacksonville because of a hamstring injury. Battle, a third-round pick of the Bengals in the 2023 NFL Draft out of Alabama, is in his fourth NFL season with Cincinnati. He played in all 51 of the Bengals' games over his first three seasons, recording six interceptions and making 30 starts. On his 25th birthday , Battle had an interception of Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson during the second quarter of the Cincinnati's NFL Week 15 loss . Battle was injured during the fourth quarter of the Bengals' Week 13 loss to Pittsburgh last season. During the 2024 season, Battle recovered a fumble and returned it during the third quarter of the Bengals' NFL Week 15 win against Tennessee, but Battle lost the ball just shy of the goal line through the back of the end zone for a touchback. Play-by-play announcer Mike Tirico missed the Week 9 Sunday night game between the Bucs and Bears in Chicago because of a health issue . Noah Eagle called the Bucs-Bears game with Collinsworth and sideline reporter Melissa Stark. NBC Sports analyst Devin McCourty said during the week that he was eager to see the reception for former Pittsburgh head coach Mike Tomlin at Paycor Stadium. "I'm excited to see if Mike Tomlin gets booed this week, if people hate him, or are throwing things at him," McCourty told reporters Nov. 11. In 2024, Tirico referred to the tackle then- Bengals linebacker Logan Wilson made in 2023 of Ravens tight end Mark Andrews as a "hip-drop tackle." In an exclusive Q&A in 2022 with The Enquirer, Tirico talked about working with Collinsworth, why the Wild Card Playoff win against the Las Vegas Raiders was the most memorable Bengals game he's called, and his long-time friendship with Bengals radio play-by-play announcer Dan Hoard. This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: Collinsworth slams Jordan Battle for Bengals-Steelers taunting penalty

item.title: St. Charles falls in OHSAA Division I boys soccer state final
item.description: Another deep tournament run ended in unfortunately familiar fashion for the St. Charles soccer team. The Cardinals almost tripled Kettering Fairmont in shots and earned a handful of quality scoring chances in the Division I boys state final Nov. 15 at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field, but the first-time state finalist Firebirds converted a higher percentage of opportunities and came away with a 3-1 win. Senior forward Sam Lofthouse scored St. Charles’ only goal, spinning and shooting from about 25 yards to the right of the goal with 25:35 to play and sneaking his shot into the upper right corner. That made it 2-1, but Fairmont (15-5-3) got the goal back less than four minutes later. Gavin Weaver’s corner kick got all the way through traffic, and Luke Davidson put it in from right in front. Azariyah Nsabimama and Aaron Black scored 12 minutes apart in the first half for Fairmont, and St. Charles lost for only the fourth time this season (18-4-1) and first since its regular-season finale Oct. 15 against Worthington Kilbourne. St. Charles, appearing in its 12th state tournament, fourth in a row and seeking its first title since 1985, outshot Fairmont 23-8. The Cardinals also were state runners-up in 2024, 2016, 1991, 1988 and 1981. St. Charles had outscored its first five tournament opponents 15-3, including a 1-0 win over defending state champion Dublin Jerome in a state semifinal in which Lofthouse had the only goal. Cardinals sophomore goalie Micah Neil made three saves. Fairmont’s Carson Dewald stopped six shots. This story will be updated. High school sports reporter Dave Purpura can be reached at dpurpura@dispatch.com and at @dp_dispatch on X. This article originally appeared on The Columbus Dispatch: St. Charles falls in OHSAA Division I boys soccer state final

item.title: Jayson Tatum offers honest Cooper Flagg outlook after Celtics blast Mavericks
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Winslow Townson-Imagn Images Jayson Tatum offers honest Cooper Flagg outlook after Celtics blast Mavericks appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Celtics have exceeded expectations with their 11-2 start to the current NBA season. Their latest victory was a 131-94 triumph over the Dallas Mavericks and that game allowed the Celtics to move into first place in the Atlantic Division. The Celtics have a one-half game lead over the Philadelphia 76ers. Most expected the Celtics to lose some of their luster after trading superstar Jaylen Brown to the Sixers and installing veteran Paul George into the lineup. Instead, George has been healthy and has been a solid fit in head coach Joe Mazzulla’s rotation. The win over the Mavericks saw the Celtics build a 42-9 lead at the conclusion of the first quarter. That was Boston’s largest lead at the end of the opening quarter in team history. It was the best performance of an NBA team in the first quarter since the Los Angeles Lakers outscored the Sacramento Kings 40-4 in 1987. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Celtics were led by Jayson Tatum , who scored 32 points and added 6 rebounds and 6 assists. He made 11 of 18 field goal attempts, and he was successful on 5 of 8 3-point attempts. Derrick White supplemented Tatum’s production with 16 points and 4 rebounds. Second-year star Cooper Flagg had 17 points for the Mavericks (7-7), and he caught Tatum’s eye with his showing. “I think what he’s done thus far in the league has been incredible,” Tatum said , per Celtics beat reporter Daniel Donabedian. “So it’s going to be fun to watch him as his career continues to grow. “As he gets older, the game is just going to continue to slow down (for him).”

item.title: LeBron James reveals hilarious adjustment 76ers teammates had to endure with him
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images LeBron James reveals hilarious adjustment 76ers teammates had to endure with him appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . 14 games into the Philadelphia 76ers ’ 2026-27 season, LeBron James says his new teammates are still adjusting to playing alongside the future Hall of Fame forward. James surpassed Jason Kidd on the all-time assists list, a facet of his game he has undoubtedly sharpened throughout his 24-year career. In doing so, he’s emerged as a point-forward role for Philadelphia, leading the team in assists with 6.5 per game. 76ers second-year guard VJ Edgecombe is still getting used to his new teammate, James said, per ESPN’s Kris Rhim. “You can ask VJ [Edgecombe] for sure. I hit VJ a couple of times; there were a couple of times he didn’t finish his route in practice early on in training camp,” James said. “I told him, even when you don’t think you’re open, you’re going to be open.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) LeBron James said that his new teammates adjusted to his passes by necessity, after James "hit them in the head a couple times. “You can ask VJ [Edgecombe] for sure. I hit VJ a couple times.” pic.twitter.com/hAKZX25yue — Kris Rhim (@krisrhim1) November 15, 2026 76ers’ LeBron James finished with 15 points, 11 assists, seven rebounds, and one block in a 131-124 win against the Indiana Pacers on Sunday. Jaylen Brown led the Sixers with 31 points, as seven players finished in double figures, including Tyrese Maxey, who scored 27 points on 9-for-19 shooting, plus six assists, four rebounds, and one steal. Anfree Simons and Dean Wade both led the bench with a dozen points each. The 76ers improved to 11-3, trailing the Boston Celtics by only 0.5 games for first place in the Eastern Conference standings. The Celtics handed the Sixers one of their worst regular-season losses, 123-101, to take the top spot on Tuesday. The 76ers will visit the Brooklyn Nets on the second leg of a back-to-back on Monday. Related: 76ers’ LeBron James reacts to passing Jason Kidd on NBA’s all-time assists list Related: 76ers’ LeBron James earns comparison to ‘AI machine’ by Rick Carlisle

item.title: 'You live for them, you play for them' - Auston Trusty honors late father with goal on emotional USMNT return
item.description: Auston Trusty GFX - GOAL In his first match since his father’s death, Auston Trusty scored against Haiti and found comfort in the teammates he calls family. The goal was only part of the story. MIAMI -- For one brief moment, Auston Trusty's sadness subsided, and his competitiveness took over. As he ran towards the corner flag after scoring his second U.S. Men's National Team goal, Trusty got caught up in the moment. He cupped his hands and stared at the crowd full of Haitian fans just seconds after giving his side a 1-0 lead. And then, as he ran back to his spot on the field, he remembered. The goal faded and reality set in. As happy as he was with his finish, Trusty was still adjusting to a new reality, one without the man he looked up to most. Saturday’s game was Trusty’s first since his father, Walt, passed away on Oct. 19. The weeks since have been difficult, to say the least. Celtic granted him time away to grieve, and he joined USMNT camp directly after attending his father’s funeral. Saturday marked his return to competitive action. It was fitting, then, that Trusty was the first USMNT player to find a moment of joy against Haiti. It didn't fix anything, and it won't, but Trusty's early goal brought peace and comfort to a man who has spent the last few weeks searching for just that. "I'm just honored to represent him," Trusty said postgame, "and play with his last name and showcase for him. I want to showcase to the world what I can do for him and his glory. I'm just very proud to score today and have a good game." Even in a 6-0 win where goals blend, Trusty's goal stood out. It was, as he said, a tribute to something bigger. More specifically, it was a tribute to someone who meant so much to him. A difficult time Unless you’ve experienced it, it’s hard to grasp the emotional toll of losing a parent. Trusty has spent the past few weeks grappling with that loss alongside his family in Pennsylvania. Walt Trusty, like his son, was a standout athlete. Back home in Media, Pa., he was a history-making basketball player in the late 60s and early 70s. As his playing days ended, his fandom remained, as he supported the local Philadelphia teams. More importantly, he also supported his children. He had six of them, and Auston was his youngest. As Trusty blossomed as a soccer star, first locally and then in Europe, the centerback's father was there every step of the way. Just this summer, he was able to watch on as his son played in, and scored in, a World Cup. "The past few weeks have been very, very tough," Trusty said on Saturday, reflecting on his father's impact on his life. "Probably the toughest of my life. Losing my father, it's never easy losing a parent, but you live for them, you play for them. He was very influential for me growing up, and also put me in the position I'm in today." On Saturday, Trusty was named to the starting XI for the USMNT. It was his first game since Oct. 15, four days before his father's passing. It didn't take long

"I'm just honored to represent him," Trusty said postgame, "and play with his last name and showcase for him. I want to showcase to the world what I can do for him and his glory. I'm just very proud to score today and have a good game." Even in a 6-0 win where goals blend, Trusty's goal stood out. It was, as he said, a tribute to something bigger. More specifically, it was a tribute to someone who meant so much to him. A difficult time Unless you’ve experienced it, it’s hard to grasp the emotional toll of losing a parent. Trusty has spent the past few weeks grappling with that loss alongside his family in Pennsylvania. Walt Trusty, like his son, was a standout athlete. Back home in Media, Pa., he was a history-making basketball player in the late 60s and early 70s. As his playing days ended, his fandom remained, as he supported the local Philadelphia teams. More importantly, he also supported his children. He had six of them, and Auston was his youngest. As Trusty blossomed as a soccer star, first locally and then in Europe, the centerback's father was there every step of the way. Just this summer, he was able to watch on as his son played in, and scored in, a World Cup. "The past few weeks have been very, very tough," Trusty said on Saturday, reflecting on his father's impact on his life. "Probably the toughest of my life. Losing my father, it's never easy losing a parent, but you live for them, you play for them. He was very influential for me growing up, and also put me in the position I'm in today." On Saturday, Trusty was named to the starting XI for the USMNT. It was his first game since Oct. 15, four days before his father's passing. It didn't take long for Trusty to make an impact, either, despite all he'd been through. A fitting tribute Trusty got everything right as he scored a memorable goal, although the celebration didn't quite go to plan. The defender played all 90 minutes in the USMNT's 6-0 win. It was the first goal that was the most important, though, in more ways than one. In the 10th minute, the USMNT earned a free kick a few yards outside of the box. Sebastian Berhalter stepped up to hit it. The midfielder's free kick went over the Haiti defense and right onto the foot of Trusty. The defender made no mistake, placing his shot into the back of the net first-time. The emotion came over him, but not in the way he expected. "I thought before the game, 'Okay, if I score, I'll do this'," he said. "I don't know what happened, but I did the good old [hand cupping] just because it's the beginning of the game, they're loud, and they had a chance, and they thought they had something. So just me being competitive, I did that. "Then after, when I was running back, I said, 'Dang, why didn't I do something?' Next goal...To score that goal and also to have the win today. It really meant a lot." Celebration or no celebration, by the end of the match, Trusty had come to terms with the moment. He knew what it represented, both for himself and for his grieving family. It also meant something to his found family, too, as they've supported him through his tough time. The USMNT family Trusty is surrounded by familiar faces when he joins the USMNT The USMNT are filled with people Trusty has known for most of his life. He met Mark McKenzie and Matt Freese as kids coming up with the Philadelphia Union. There are 11 players in the current squad that he battled alongside this summer during the World Cup. In that sense, the national team is a second family, one that has been there for some of Trusty's best and worst moments. This month is undeniably one of the worst and, in that moment, Trusty says the USMNT have stepped up. That's what families do, after all. "These guys in my family," he said. "I've known them for a very long time, from the staff to the players, so it's just coming into a nice, warm environment that's very welcoming and very understanding of the situation. "They're all my brothers, so if I'm hurting inside, they're hurting as well. I'm really happy to come back here as my first stop." 'It means a lot' Saturday's gameball will be among the most heartfelt mementos Trusty receives during his career. After the match, the USMNT gathered in the locker room. Captain Tyler Adams stepped up, holding the game ball. "Trusty, there are some things bigger than soccer, man," he said in a moment showcased by the USMNT's social media. "The way that you played tonight, obviously getting a goal, it just means a lot. The federation is obviously behind you, the team is behind you. I just want to recognize you with this, man." Trusty stepped up, composed, and grabbed a game ball that will feel different than any he'd received before. This wasn't just commemorating a goal; it was, in a way, commemorating a person and a lifetime. "Thank you. It means a lot," a visibly emotional Trusty said. "Obviously it's not easy losing your father, but to come here and represent the country, represent all you guys, it really means a lot to me." "I don't want to cry," he added, fighting back tears," but thank you, guys, very much, and I appreciate it." Trusty may have forgotten the celebration he had planned, but Saturday’s game will be one he never forgets. It was his first match since losing his father, a first step forward through a grief still fresh. There will be more moments in a USMNT shirt, and more moments with that Trusty name on the back. Maybe next time, he’ll remember the celebration. On Saturday, though, he didn’t need one to make it clear who he was playing for.

item.title: Are Chiefs Leading the AFC West? Examining Where They Stand
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - NOVEMBER 15: Josh Downs #12 and Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs celebrate a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty The Kansas City Chiefs got a huge 35-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 10. Despite some key injuries, Kansas City’s offense put up 461 total yards and found the endzone five times. The Chiefs’ defense had Atlanta’s offense stifled all game long. With nine games down and eight to go, the standings are becoming intricate. Kansas City Chiefs Own Tiebreaker Over Denver Broncos for AFC West Lead Notable for the AFC West tiebreakers. Chiefs and Broncos split, next tiebreaker is divisional record. KC is 3-1, Denver 2-1. KC currently in first by this tiebreaker Second tiebreaker is common games. Aside from AFCW, Broncos are 3-1, KC 2-1. Chiefs are 6-1 in AFC, and Broncos… — Matt Derrick (@mattderrick) November 15, 2026 With the Broncos on their bye in Week 10, and the Chiefs already having theirs back in Week 5, the teams are finally even in games played. Both are sitting at a 7-2 record, with one head-to-head win over each other. Having split the season series , the tiebreaker then moves to best divisional record. That is where Kansas City has the advantage, owning a 3-1 AFC West record, with Denver at 2-1. The caveat is that the Broncos have played one less divisional game. Denver has two remaining against the Las Vegas Raiders, and one against the Los Angeles Chargers. The Chiefs have one matchup a piece left against the Raiders and Chargers. For now, however, Kansas City has the slight edge. Here are the teams that would be in the postseason if it began today: Buffalo Bills (8-1) Kansas City Chiefs (7-2) Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2) Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) Denver Broncos (7-2)* Cincinnati Bengals (6-2)* Cleveland Browns (6-4)* *=Wildcard Chiefs Have Tougher Road Than Broncos to Division Title Unfortunately for Kansas City, its remaining schedule is much tougher than Denver’s. The Chiefs have a brutal stretch from Week 12-16, which includes matchups against the Bills, Los Angeles Rams, Bengals, Patriots, and San Francisco 49ers. Three of those five games will be on the road. As for the Broncos, just two of their remaining eight games are against teams that currently have a winning record — the Steelers in Week 12, and the Bills in Week 16. The rest of their opponents include the Miami Dolphins, New York Jets, Patriots, Raiders, and Chargers. The Chiefs will conclude the season with a road game against the Chargers in Week 17, and a home matchup against the Raiders in Week 18. Depending on how well they survive the stretch that proceeds that, those could be must-win games. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Are Chiefs Leading the AFC West? Examining Where They Stand appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Mendoza will need to be a quick learner
item.description: Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza (15) throws the ball in the fourth quarter against the Seattle Seahawks at Allegiant Stadium. LAS VEGAS — Mendoza Time finally arrived Sunday at Allegiant Stadium. But it sure looked the Las Vegas Raiders were still on Cousins Time, particularly in the second half. With Kirk Cousins having been traded to Minnesota Tuesday at the NFL trade deadline, Fernando Mendoza was able to stop talking about being a starting quarterback in the National Football League and actually play the role. The NFL’s No. 1 overall draft pick from April was ready to go as the Raiders looked to get back to .500 as the second half of the season got underway. Mendoza turned in a poised performance, running for a 10-yard touchdown and giving the Raiders a fighting chance against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks, who boast the NFL’s top defense. He would finish 17 for 29 passing and 143 yards. Mendoza also ran for 22 yards and the first-quarter TD. But with Brock Bowers, his best weapon out for the majority of the contest and the Seahawks bringing the heat, Mendoza’s debut ultimately resulted in a 21-13 loss to Seattle as the Raiders dropped their second straight and fell to 4-6. “I can’t thank everybody enough for all the ‘apoyo’ which is support in Spanish, especially all the fans and my teammates, my coaches who had a lot of support in me, giving me this opportunity and chance,” Mendoza said. “I need to be better for them. “However, it’s always great to get the experience of a first NFL start and now have more tangible items to improve off of and see the deficiencies, then attack them this week.” “He was well prepared,” Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said of Mendoza. “He started the game really well. Overall, for his first start, I thought it was a good start.” The Raiders decided to use one of George Allen’s lines in proclaiming the Mendoza Era — “The Future Is Now” — and that’s all well and good. He was going to debut as the team’s starter at some point so why not attach a tag to it? These days, it seems it’s all in the marketing and social media details. Mendoza received a huge ovation from the crowd of 62,624 when he as introduced with the offensive starters prior to kickoff. It must have been quite a rush for him. And when he capped the first drive as a starter with a 10-yard TD run, well, elation probably doesn’t quite cover what he felt. Was he perfect? Not quite. item.content:encoded: Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza (15) throws the ball in the fourth quarter against the Seattle Seahawks at Allegiant Stadium. LAS VEGAS — Mendoza Time finally arrived Sunday at Allegiant Stadium. But it sure looked the Las Vegas Raiders were still on Cousins Time, particularly in the second half. With Kirk Cousins having been traded to Minnesota Tuesday at the NFL trade deadline, Fernando Mendoza was able to stop talking about being a starting quarterback in the National Football League and actually play the role. The NFL’s No. 1 overall draft pick from April was ready to go as the Raiders looked to get back to .500 as the second half of the season got underway. Mendoza turned in a poised performance, running for a 10-yard touchdown and giving the Raiders a fighting chance against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks, who boast the NFL’s top defense. He would finish 17 for 29 passing and 143 yards. Mendoza also ran for 22 yards and the first-quarter TD. But with Brock Bowers, his best weapon out for the majority of the contest and the Seahawks bringing the heat, Mendoza’s debut ultimately resulted in a 21-13 loss to Seattle as the Raiders dropped their second straight and fell to 4-6. “I can’t thank everybody enough for all the ‘apoyo’ which is support in Spanish, especially all the fans and my teammates, my coaches who had a lot of support in me, giving me this opportunity and chance,” Mendoza said. “I need to be better for them. “However, it’s always great to get the experience of a first NFL start and now have more tangible items to improve off of and see the deficiencies, then attack them this week.” “He was well prepared,” Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said of Mendoza. “He started the game really well. Overall, for his first start, I thought it was a good start.” The Raiders decided to use one of George Allen’s lines in proclaiming the Mendoza Era — “The Future Is Now” — and that’s all well and good. He was going to debut as the team’s starter at some point so why not attach a tag to it? These days, it seems it’s all in the marketing and social media details. Mendoza received a huge ovation from the crowd of 62,624 when he as introduced with the offensive starters prior to kickoff. It must have been quite a rush for him. And when he capped the first drive as a starter with a 10-yard TD run, well, elation probably doesn’t quite cover what he felt. Was he perfect? Not quite. The Seahawks were determined to not let him dominate. They sacked him six times and harassed him plenty, which is what the Legion of Boom does to opposing quarterbacks. But he also displayed great poise and confidence, at least in the first half as he helped lead the Raiders to a 10-7 halftime lead. He kept drives going which greatly helped the Raiders’ defense get sufficient rest. And credit Kubiak and offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko for their game plan and play-calling. They didn’t put Mendoza in a lot of high-risk situations where he could fail. He completed his first seven passes and looked like he had a command of the offense. The second half? Mendoza and the Raiders struggled mightily. Five straight drives of three-and-out for minus-17 yards in total offense before getting untracked sort of late in the game. Once the Raiders fell behind and started chasing the game, that cautious play-calling went out the window. Yes, the Raiders still continue to struggle in running the ball effectively. They managed just 65 yards on the ground. And when they lost Bowers to an ankle injury, there went one of Mendoza’s top targets. But Mendoza showed an ability to adjust. One good thing about being a second-string quarterback, you get to work with second-string receivers in practice every day. So he had a familiarity with Jack Bech and Cody White and he got the ball to both of them for first downs during the second quarter. Now that he’s the QB1, Mendoza will hopefully find a comfort zone with Michael Mayer, Tre Tucker and Jalen Nailor along with Bowers. Still, the same problems that plagued the Silver and Black when Cousins was the starting quarterback were in play with Mendoza at the controls. The offensive line failed to hold up. The run game was stagnant. And when Mendoza had time, which wasn’t often, he was unable to connect downfield with his receivers. For Mendoza, there’ll certainly be better days. But when your line doesn’t block for you and you’re unable to run the ball and teams are pressuring you into being uncomfortable, what are you supposed to do? Throw in the fact the Seahawks were able to move the ball as Drew Lock and Jaxon Smith-Njigba did plenty of damage together and it was a story we’ve seen numerous times this year. JSN caught eight passes for 171 yards, including a 71-yard TD in the third quarter as Seattle took control of the game. So we’ll see what happens a week from now in Denver. Mendoza will undoubtedly learn from the experience. He certainly learned that life as a rookie starting quarterback in the NFL is no picnic. “It’s good to get punched in the face, because now it’s a great opportunity to grow and learn and unveil all the deficiencies that I have in my game and as a future hopeful leader of this offense,”Mendoza said. Kubiak was more succinct. “We have to play better,” he said “We got to support (Mendoza) better.” Yes and yes.

item.title: There Goes Jaden McDaniels’ New Freedom
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Jaden McDaniels had been enjoying a different view of the Timberwolves’ defense. With Jaylen Clark taking on more responsibility against opposing guards, McDaniels could spend additional possessions surveying the floor, calling out screens and helping teammates. He described the role as being a quarterback, with a clearer picture of everything developing around him. Now Minnesota must adjust without the teammate helping make that possible. Clark suffered a right hamstring strain during Saturday’s loss to Chicago and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, according to Jace Frederick of the Pioneer Press . He left the game after just three minutes. The evaluation is a checkpoint rather than a confirmed return date. For now, it leaves Minnesota without an important perimeter defender while Anthony Edwards and Donte DiVincenzo remain sidelined. Oct 16, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Minnesota Timberwolves guard Jaylen Clark (7) grabs a rebound against the Chicago Bulls during the first half at United Center. Mandatory Credit: David Banks-Imagn Images Clark’s absence also interrupts a partnership both he and McDaniels had recently explained. At Tuesday’s practice, McDaniels discussed how Clark and Ayo Dosunmu handling more assignments on the ball allowed him to contribute elsewhere. He could help rebound and alert teammates when a screen was approaching. “Really just being like a quarterback,” McDaniels said . That perspective changes when a defender is occupied with the player directly in front of him. “It’s a little easier when you can see everything instead of you being on ball and you’re just focused on the person you’re guarding,” he explained. McDaniels remains comfortable in either role. Minnesota will continue to need his length and mobility against dangerous scorers. Clark’s availability had given Chris Finch another option for distributing those responsibilities. Losing that option could pull McDaniels toward more possessions defending the initial action, reducing some of the opportunities to read and influence what happens behind it. Clark understood the benefit his work provided. Credit: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images During Wednesday’s practice, he described his assignment as bringing energy, picking up opponents full court and giving McDaniels a break. item.content:encoded: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Jaden McDaniels had been enjoying a different view of the Timberwolves’ defense. With Jaylen Clark taking on more responsibility against opposing guards, McDaniels could spend additional possessions surveying the floor, calling out screens and helping teammates. He described the role as being a quarterback, with a clearer picture of everything developing around him. Now Minnesota must adjust without the teammate helping make that possible. Clark suffered a right hamstring strain during Saturday’s loss to Chicago and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, according to Jace Frederick of the Pioneer Press . He left the game after just three minutes. The evaluation is a checkpoint rather than a confirmed return date. For now, it leaves Minnesota without an important perimeter defender while Anthony Edwards and Donte DiVincenzo remain sidelined. Oct 16, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Minnesota Timberwolves guard Jaylen Clark (7) grabs a rebound against the Chicago Bulls during the first half at United Center. Mandatory Credit: David Banks-Imagn Images Clark’s absence also interrupts a partnership both he and McDaniels had recently explained. At Tuesday’s practice, McDaniels discussed how Clark and Ayo Dosunmu handling more assignments on the ball allowed him to contribute elsewhere. He could help rebound and alert teammates when a screen was approaching. “Really just being like a quarterback,” McDaniels said . That perspective changes when a defender is occupied with the player directly in front of him. “It’s a little easier when you can see everything instead of you being on ball and you’re just focused on the person you’re guarding,” he explained. McDaniels remains comfortable in either role. Minnesota will continue to need his length and mobility against dangerous scorers. Clark’s availability had given Chris Finch another option for distributing those responsibilities. Losing that option could pull McDaniels toward more possessions defending the initial action, reducing some of the opportunities to read and influence what happens behind it. Clark understood the benefit his work provided. Credit: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images During Wednesday’s practice, he described his assignment as bringing energy, picking up opponents full court and giving McDaniels a break. The goal was to help Minnesota use more of its teammate’s abilities. “I think he’s better when he can go score and everything as well and roam around, block shots and everything,” Clark said . “Because having to guard the best player and asking him to get 20, that’s a tough job on anybody.” That balance matters with Edwards unavailable. McDaniels has additional opportunities offensively, and Minnesota benefits when his defensive workload leaves him enough energy to use them. He acknowledged that spending less time picking up the ball full court could provide a little more rest. He also expressed genuine enthusiasm for Clark receiving chances to show his defense. “I know he could guard,” McDaniels said. “He guard me all the time. He be fouling and stuff, so it’s cool. It’s good to see. I’m just happy for him.” Clark had been doing more than absorbing difficult matchups. After Thursday’s win over Dallas, Finch highlighted his ability to create possessions through steals, deflections, loose balls and disrupted inbound passes. Credit: Bruce Kluckhohn-USA TODAY Sports “He just makes plays,” Finch said . “He makes things happen.” Replacing those contributions will require decisions about assignments and combinations. Dosunmu remains available to pressure guards, while McDaniels and Jonathan Kuminga give Minnesota versatile defensive options. Finch has yet to establish publicly how he will redistribute Clark’s minutes. The timing adds another challenge. Against Chicago, Finch criticized Minnesota’s inability to contain the ball at the point of attack, along with missed off-ball movement and slow defensive reactions. Clark would have been one of the players Minnesota could turn to for pressure and disruption. His injury removes that answer as the Wolves prepare for consecutive games against Portland. McDaniels’ ability to organize and help remains valuable. The question now is how often Minnesota can position him to do it while covering the work Clark had begun taking off his shoulders. item.title: Depleted Warriors Need to Make a Trade, Analyzing 8 Potential Options
item.description: Golden State Warriors forward Graham Ike (45) backs in against San Antonio Spurs forward Harrison Barnes (40) in the second half at Frost Bank Center. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Daniel Benjamin, Editor The Golden State Warriors are in desperate need of reinforcements and have reportedly been scouring teams’ rosters for suitable options. Despite the Warriors’ injury troubles , they have been surging thanks to elite offensive production and home-cooking. Down to 13 healthy players, Golden State fell to the San Antonio Spurs , 123-85, on Friday, dropping to 8-5 on the season. The Warriors are the ninth-highest-scoring team in the league and the ninth-best offensive squad overall. The Warriors are also the fourth-best shooting team, with an effective field goal percentage of 55.4% and true shooting percentage of 59.5%. Kerr said Brandon Williams is progressing in his hamstring injury — but likely won’t play the last few games of this trip. Williams is going through a post-practice workout now and looks like he’s moving better. — Nick Friedell (@NickFriedell) November 15, 2026 Golden State has also significantly cut down on turnovers compared to last season, which has helped them tremendously on the defensive end. The Warriors are giving up the 13th-fewest points and rank 14th in defensive rating, a slight improvement over last season. However, the Dubs numbers are better than their actual defense has been. Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr looks on in the first half against the San Antonio Spurs at Frost Bank Center. Photo Credit: Daniel Dunn, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect Golden State is allowing opponents to shoot 46.1% from the field and 34% from 3-point range. The Warriors are allowing opponents to make 66.2% of their attempts from within five feet of the rim — seventh-worst — though they have done a decent job on the defensive glass and in transition defense. The Warriors have also done a strong job of avoiding fouls and forcing turnovers. The Warriors have played the eighth toughest schedule, per Power Rankings Guru. However, seven of the Warriors’ first 12 games were at home, where they are 6-1. The Warriors have the sixth-best scoring margin, with five double-digit wins, and are 3-3 on the season against teams with a .500 record. According to Tankathon, the Golden State Warriors have the 13th-toughest remaining schedule. The Warriors will also be shorthanded for the foreseeable future, with Kristaps Porzingis likely never playing again . Brandon Williams (hamstring) is out until at least November 17, and Steph Curry (strained oblique) is likely out the rest of this month and potentially longer. Steph Curry Injury Update: Like most strains, time lost for oblique strains is based on severity of the injury. The average time lost for nondescript oblique strains is 4.8 games (~13 days), but that number jumps to 16 games (~38 days) when moderate/severe strains are isolated. — Jeff Stotts (@InStreetClothes) November 12, 2026 Golde

Despite the Warriors’ injury troubles , they have been surging thanks to elite offensive production and home-cooking. Down to 13 healthy players, Golden State fell to the San Antonio Spurs , 123-85, on Friday, dropping to 8-5 on the season. The Warriors are also the fourth-best shooting team, with an effective field goal percentage of 55.4% and true shooting percentage of 59.5%. Kerr said Brandon Williams is progressing in his hamstring injury — but likely won’t play the last few games of this trip. Williams is going through a post-practice workout now and looks like he’s moving better. — Nick Friedell (@NickFriedell) November 15, 2026 Golden State has also significantly cut down on turnovers compared to last season, which has helped them tremendously on the defensive end. Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr looks on in the first half against the San Antonio Spurs at Frost Bank Center. Photo Credit: Daniel Dunn, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect Golden State is allowing opponents to shoot 46.1% from the field and 34% from 3-point range. The Warriors are allowing opponents to make 66.2% of their attempts from within five feet of the rim — seventh-worst — though they have done a decent job on the defensive glass and in transition defense. The Warriors have also done a strong job of avoiding fouls and forcing turnovers. The Warriors have played the eighth toughest schedule, per Power Rankings Guru. However, seven of the Warriors’ first 12 games were at home, where they are 6-1. The Warriors have the sixth-best scoring margin, with five double-digit wins, and are 3-3 on the season against teams with a .500 record. According to Tankathon, the Golden State Warriors have the 13th-toughest remaining schedule. The Warriors will also be shorthanded for the foreseeable future, with Kristaps Porzingis likely never playing again . Brandon Williams (hamstring) is out until at least November 17, and Steph Curry (strained oblique) is likely out the rest of this month and potentially longer. Steph Curry Injury Update: Like most strains, time lost for oblique strains is based on severity of the injury. The average time lost for nondescript oblique strains is 4.8 games (~13 days), but that number jumps to 16 games (~38 days) when moderate/severe strains are isolated. — Jeff Stotts (@InStreetClothes) November 12, 2026 Golden State Warriors player Moses Moody watches the Dallas Wings game against the Golden State Valkyries at Chase Center. Photo Credit: David Gonzales, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect Meanwhile, Moses Moody could return between December and January. Meanwhile, Jimmy Butler isn’t slated to return until February-March. However, before returning to the Warriors, he plans to play at least one game for the G League’s Santa Cruz Warriors. “It may not be for long, but I’m going to play in Santa Cruz,” Butler told Nick Friedell of The Athletic . What Do the Warriors Need and Who Are the Potential Options? Golden State has already lost 62 players to injuries. As a result, all 15 players on the Warriors’ 18-man roster have seen time with Steve Kerr, who used his ninth different starting lineup against the Spurs. Last night, Kerr had Yaxel Lendeborg, Draymond Green, De’Anthony Melton, Brandin Podziemski and Will Richard as his first unit. And it was a pure and undisputed disaster from the start. Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry (30) holds his side during the first quarter against the Houston Rockets at Toyota Center. Photo Credit: Troy Taormina, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect Golden State didn’t score a single point in the first six minutes and trailed 18-2 with 5:53 left. The Warriors trailed by 22 points after the first quarter and trailed by as many as 43 in the game. The Warriors shot 33% from the field, and their starters were outscored 67-30, with each posting a plus/minus rating of -23. They allowed the Spurs to shoot 48% from the field, were outrebounded by 17, and were outscored at the free-throw line by 9. That 18-0 Spurs run is the longest unanswered allowed by the Warriors to start a game under Steve Kerr, per @StatsWilliams. — Anthony Slater (@anthonyVslater) November 14, 2026 LJ Cryer led the way for the Warriors with 20 points, making 6-of-11 from 3-point range. Charles Bassey was the only other Dub in double figures, with 11 points and 5 rebounds. With Friday night’s loss to the Spurs, Golden State drops to 14-28 without Curry since the start of last season. But the Warriors still believe they are in a good spot. “We’re more certain of who we are, what makes us a good team,” Draymond Green said about Curry missing time a few days ago . I think that puts us in a better position to succeed without him than we were last year. Then obviously [Yaxel Lendeborg], having a guy you can give the ball to and he can create an advantage. [Brandin Podziemski] is playing a lot better. … It puts us in a better position.” Golden State Warriors forward Yaxel Lendeborg (1) shoots over San Antonio Spurs center Luke Kornet (7) in the first half at Frost Bank Center. Photo Credit: Daniel Dunn, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect While Curry is out, Golden State plans to ride Lendeborg. Lendeborg is off to a strong start to the season, averaging 20.2 points, 7.4 rebounds, 3.5 assists, and 1.0 steals while shooting 48.6/41.4/73.7. He also has produced three double-doubles. “We’re for sure going to go to him and ask him to create advantages for us and create shots.” Steve Kerr on what will be expected of Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg. https://t.co/UfonwIddQS — Joseph Dycus (@joseph_dycus) November 14, 2026 However, the Warriors need some reinforcements. Here is a look at what their main needs are and possible options. Warriors Need A Starting Center and Size Overall In the Frontcourt With Porzingis having stepped away from basketball, Golden State doesn’t have a starting-caliber center, leaving Green, Al Horford, Charles Bassey, and Graham Ike to man the middle. Ike, on a two-way contract, is the only player at least 6-10. The Warriors rank in the bottom half of the league in efficiency difference, per Hoopstats. While the Warriors’ center group has been decent defensively, they have been getting hammered at the four. Part of the problem is their lack of overall size and players playing out of position. But the Warriors’ five-man group is one of the worst in the league offensively. Among centers, the Warriors rank 26th in points per game at 15.8 on 48.8% shooting from the field. They also rank in the bottom third of the league in rebounds and don’t get to the free-throw line. On the positive side, they are an excellent passing group, averaging 7.8 assists per game (second-most in the league). Who Are Options For The Warriors At Center The good news is that Golden State does have plenty of options. Chicago Bulls big men Nic Claxton and Jalen Smith have been linked to the Warriors. Isaiah Stewart, Brook Lopez, and Myles Turner are also potential options. Nic Claxton Chicago Bulls center Nic Claxton (9) lies on the court after trying for a basket against the San Antonio Spurs during the first half at United Center. Photo Credit: Matt Marton, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect Claxton has been linked to the Warriors for the last couple of seasons. The 27-year-old big man recently made his season de

item.title: Yaxel Lendeborg Shaves Head After Worst Game Of NBA Career
item.description: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 11: Yaxel Lendeborg #1 of the Golden State Warriors reacts during the third quarter of the game against the Houston Rockets at Toyota Center on November 11, 2026 in Houston, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) Getty The Golden State Warriors will witness a new look for rookie Yaxel Lendeborg next game after he shaved most of his fair. NBA fans took note of Lendeborg’s frustration in the team’s first game after Stephen Curry’s recent injury. Curry is going to miss at least two weeks and saw the Warriors getting destroyed by the San Antonio Spurs on Friday night without him. Yaxel delivered an NBA career low 3 points on 1 of 13 shooting to end his hot streak. View this post on Instagram Today showed Lendeborg with a low hair cut after cutting his hair on Saturday after the loss. Comments about feeling mentally frustrated against Victor Wembanyama was the first real sign of rookie struggles for Yaxel in his outstanding season so far. The hair cut signifies his desire for change and rebuilding after the Spurs exposed his flaws. The injury to Curry puts Lendeborg in a tough spot as the top offensive option on the team. Fellow injured players Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody missing time destroys any change of roster depth without Curry. Yaxel must continue his hot start to help the Warriors get through this difficult period. The limited options places more pressure on the exciting rookie. Steve Kerr Comments On New Yaxel Lendeborg Look Warriors head coach Steve Kerr took it as a positive that Yaxel has taken the poor performance personally. Kerr knows winning habits between his Golden State coaching stint and championships as a player with the Chicago Bulls and Spurs. The haircut was more meaningful than just someone wanting a fresh look, according to Kerr: “He chopped all his hair off. I didn’t even recognize him. So apparently that’s his response to getting beat by 40, is to go right to the barber.” Both Kerr and Lendeborg have been praised for the Warriors’ strong start to the season. Most expected Golden State to be a bottom feeder team, especially after Kristaps Porzingis was ruled out in training camp over his illness. Yaxel has given them a second star behind Curry, and Kerr’s rotations and game plans have made up the gap against teams with better talent. item.title: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs protest in Prague over public media funding plan
item.description: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs rallied in Prague on Sunday against government plans to replace public media fees with direct state funding, which critics say threatens broadcasters’ independence. Organisers said turnout exceeded a March protest of more than 200,000, potentially making it the largest demonstration since the 1989 Velvet Revolution.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Lakers’ Luka Doncic gives ‘amazing player’ his flowers after torching Suns
item.description: Danielle Cortez-Imagn Images Lakers’ Luka Doncic gives ‘amazing player’ his flowers after torching Suns appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Lakers rolled to their eighth straight win after beating the Phoenix Suns, 131-123 , at PHX Arena on Sunday, with Luka Doncic delivering another masterful performance. Doncic exploded for 43 points on 13-of-28 shooting, including 5-of-13 from long distance. He added three rebounds and nine assists. The Lakers improved to 12-2, tied with the San Antonio Spurs for the best record in the Western Conference. With Austin Reaves sidelined by a heel injury , Quentin Grimes filled the void with 22 points on 7-of-10 shooting, including 5-of-6 from rainbow territory, six rebounds, and two steals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Doncic saluted Grimes for stepping up , as reported by Lakers Today’s Raj Chipalu. “He’s becoming himself again. We really need that. He’s an amazing player. He’s going to help us a lot, and tonight he showed what kind of player he is,” said the six-time All-Star. The Lakers acquired Grimes in the offseason, signing him to a four-year, $60 million contract. The team envisioned him as a perfect fit alongside Doncic and Reaves with his two-way acumen. Grimes, however, has been struggling with consistency. Before the game against the Suns, he was averaging 8.0 points, 2.5 rebounds, and 2.5 assists. If Reaves continues to miss time, the 26-year-old Grimes will get more opportunities. He has shown he can produce on both ends, and Doncic’s vote of confidence should bode well for him. Grimes may have found a home with the Lakers after playing for four teams—the New York Knicks, the Detroit Pistons, the Dallas Mavericks, and the Philadelphia 76ers—in five years. Related: Lakers’ Collin Sexton keeps it real on fans’ ‘MVP’ chants for Luka Doncic on the road Related: Luka Doncic puts Lakers on notice after Suns’ fourth quarter rally

item.title: Everything Texans QB C.J. Stroud said after Week 10 loss to Browns
item.description: Here's everything Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud said following a 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 10, including his thoughts on the Texans' outlook beyond Sunday's loss. Question: What do you feel like changed the most there from the first half to the second half? C.J. Stroud: “They just started pressuring and getting sticky in coverage. We really didn’t adjust to it. We gotta do a better job coming out in the second half and finding ways to move the ball and get points.” Q: The momentum shift- did you guys kinda feel like, “we had it.” And then it starts to slip away? Stroud: “That’s football. It’s a four-quarter game. They’ve come back on a lot of teams this season and won a lot of games with two-minute drives. We knew what it was. We were just dead. We gotta find a way to execute and create more energy on the sideline and keep things going." Q: DeMeco [Ryans] was talking about the penalty issue. It’ll get better, and then it keeps coming up. As a team leader, what do you see from your perspective on the penalties? Stroud: “We gotta play better as players. There’s a lot of things where we don’t need the penalty. We’ll take if you get beat just let the guy go on special teams, or the false starts, we gotta fix that. I don’t know all the other penalties we had but those are the main ones that I thought affected the game. I have the utmost hope and faith in Tae [Ersery] and whatever happened on special teams, the guys getting it fixed. The time is now. We gotta be moreurgent because time is running out.” Q: What made it difficult for you guys to adjust to some of the pressure and them being stickier in coverage? Stroud: “Honestly I don’t know. We gotta find ways to protect it, because guys are open on the back end. That’s what I think a lot of teams will do. They’ll just pressure and try to say, ‘you gotta make a big play.’ I think we gotta be able to not just run two to three routes, widen our route tree, and just run by people sometimes, and do it more often. Gotta find ways to win tough games. This is November. It’s playoff time already. We put ourselves in position to win. No matter how it looks, we gotta find a way to win the game.” Q: With getting behind on early downs, third-and-longs, and penalties, was that the most frustrating part of the loss today? Stroud: “I mean it’s frustrating losing at the end of the day. We’ve had a lot of close games and we haven’t found a way to win those games. That’s the tough part I believe. At the end of the day, I gotta look myself in the mirror. I had the third down to Dalton [Schultz] that I missed a little high. If we stay on the field right there, we burn some more of their timeouts and burn some more clock. That’s an impact play that I could’ve made that I gotta be better. I think with all of our tape, we just got some messy stuff that we gotta clean up. Gotta do it quick. Quick turnaround.” This article originally appeared on Texans Wire: Everything Texans QB C.J. We gotta do a better job coming out in the second half and finding ways to move the ball and get points.” Q: The momentum shift- did you guys kinda feel like, “we had it.” And then it starts to slip away? Stroud: “That’s football. It’s a four-quarter game. They’ve come back on a lot of teams this season and won a lot of games with two-minute drives. We knew what it was. We were just dead. We gotta find a way to execute and create more energy on the sideline and keep things going." Q: DeMeco [Ryans] was talking about the penalty issue. It’ll get better, and then it keeps coming up. As a team leader, what do you see from your perspective on the penalties? Stroud: “We gotta play better as players. There’s a lot of things where we don’t need the penalty. We’ll take if you get beat just let the guy go on special teams, or the false starts, we gotta fix that. I don’t know all the other penalties we had but those are the main ones that I thought affected the game. I have the utmost hope and faith in Tae [Ersery] and whatever happened on special teams, the guys getting it fixed. The time is now. We gotta be moreurgent because time is running out.” Q: What made it difficult for you guys to adjust to some of the pressure and them being stickier in coverage? Stroud: “Honestly I don’t know. We gotta find ways to protect it, because guys are open on the back end. That’s what I think a lot of teams will do. They’ll just pressure and try to say, ‘you gotta make a big play.’ I think we gotta be able to not just run two to three routes, widen our route tree, and just run by people sometimes, and do it more often. Gotta find ways to win tough games. This is November. It’s playoff time already. We put ourselves in position to win. No matter how it looks, we gotta find a way to win the game.” Q: With getting behind on early downs, third-and-longs, and penalties, was that the most frustrating part of the loss today? Stroud: “I mean it’s frustrating losing at the end of the day. We’ve had a lot of close games and we haven’t found a way to win those games. That’s the tough part I believe. At the end of the day, I gotta look myself in the mirror. I had the third down to Dalton [Schultz] that I missed a little high. If we stay on the field right there, we burn some more of their timeouts and burn some more clock. That’s an impact play that I could’ve made that I gotta be better. I think with all of our tape, we just got some messy stuff that we gotta clean up. Gotta do it quick. Quick turnaround.” This article originally appeared on Texans Wire: Everything Texans QB C.J. Stroud said after Week 10 loss to Browns

item.title: Cowboys’ Brian Schottenheimer hits with new low after getting thumped by 49ers
item.description: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Cowboys’ Brian Schottenheimer hits with new low after getting thumped by 49ers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . While owner Jerry Jones was hoping to see the Dallas Cowboys upset the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, it didn’t end up happening, as the franchise experienced another disappointing loss to the NFC foe in a shootout, 46-40. As speculation continues around Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer and his job security, this latest statistic coming out of the loss to the 49ers is one that fans won’t want to hear. Noted by Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram, Dallas under Schottenheimer has not beaten an NFC team once since he became the head coach in 2025. The Cowboys are now 0-9-1 against NFC teams not in their division under Brian Schottenheimer ,” Harris wrote on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) There’s no doubt that statistic is much more frustrating after the loss to the 49ers, where the offense was firing on all cylinders as Dak Prescott threw for five touchdowns ( George Pickens caught three of them) and one interception with 343 yards. However, the defense allowed the 49ers to score 14 points in the third quarter and 15 points in the final period to close out the contest. Jones would say on 105.3 The Fan on Friday that they “still like” Dallas’ “bet” on Schottenheimer. “Given the ability to live to tell about it, Brian will be a year from now, two years from now, three years from now, he’ll be much more (prepared) for the kinds of challenges a head coach has. There’s no question, you pay a price when you’re doing it for the first time. … I still like [our] bet [on him],” Jones said, via Jon Machota. At any rate, it remains to be seen if the Cowboys change their mind on Schottenheimer, as the head coach looks to bounce back next Sunday against the Tennessee Titans with a 4-6 record, putting them second in the NFC East. Related: Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb makes curious decision after loss to 49ers Related: Cowboys make unwanted history with horrendous defense in loss to 49ers

item.title: 'When the moment was big, he was at his best': Mike Tirico pays touching tribute to Dan Hicks
item.description: Credit: NBC Legendary sportscaster Dan Hicks died unexpectedly last week at the age of 64. Since the moment the news broke, those that worked with Hicks have been issuing remembrances of their colleague and offering condolences to those he left behind. Mike Tirico added his own tribute to the list on Sunday Night Football , and had nothing but the highest praise for Hicks. Of his style on the microphone, Tirico said Hicks was “No schtick. All substance,” and constantly making those around him better. “It’s no coincidence that some of the best sports analysts ever shined next to Hicksy,” Tirico said in a tribute package. “Meticulously prepared. A brilliant storyteller. Dan did it all. And when the moment was big, he was at his best.” Tirico also took a moment to acknowledge Hicks’s wife Hannah Storm, and the relationship they built from newsroom beginnings. “But this isn’t just the story of a great sportscaster, it’s a love story too,” Tirico said. “With his equally as talented and wonderful wife Hannah, the greatest sportscasting couple of all time. A story that started on the anchor desk at CNN, continued to NBC, and was shared with so many of us for the last 32 years.” “When the moment was big, he was at his best.” Mike Tirico honors Dan Hicks as a talented professional, family man, and true friend. https://t.co/YV0AnyCCs3 — NBC Sports (@NBCSports) November 16, 2026 Later on in the broadcast, Tirico and his partner Cris Collinsworth spoke more about their relationship with Hicks. “This has been a tough weekend for all of us at NBC. Tough for us to work tonight, after the passing of a great friend in Dan Hicks,” Tirico said. “It’s been such a sad week for so many people at NBC obviously, us included,” Collinsworth, who called NFL games alongside Hicks decades ago, added. “But you can’t help but think how much joy and how much humor that man brought to all of us. He was such a professional, but when you were around him and he was doing his impersonations, he was just so much fun, and he is dearly, dearly missed.” “That picture you see is Danny. That smile,” Tirico said. “That smile was always on his face. When he worked with people, he made everybody he worked with better. He brought out the best in his coworkers.” Mike Tirico and Cris Collinsworth remember Dan Hicks on the NBC SNF broadcast. https://t.co/tHx49I6Kpp — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 16, 2026 While Hicks may no longer be with us, several of his calls on the biggest moments in sports will last beyond any of our lifetimes. The post Mike Tirico, Cris Collinsworth pay touching tribute to Dan Hicks appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Luka Doncic Caught On Camera Taking Clipboard Away From Lakers’ Coaching Staff In Viral Incident
item.description: PHOENIX, AZ - NOVEMBER 15: Luka Doncic #77 of the Los Angeles Lakers celebrates during the game against the Phoenix Suns on November 15, 2026 at Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix, Arizona. (Photo by Barry Gossage/NBAE via Getty Images) Luka Doncic once again had a big night in the Los Angeles Lakers’ 131-123 win over the Phoenix Suns tonight. He finished with 43 points, nine assists, and three rebounds, shooting 13-28 from the field (46.4% FG) and 5-13 from beyond the arc (38.4% 3P). The Lakers held a 31-point lead near the end of the third quarter, but the Suns cut it to five points down the stretch as they made a late push to compete. In a viral incident during the fourth quarter, the broadcast caught Luka Doncic taking the clipboard away from JJ Redick and his coaching staff to draw up the team’s play to close out the game. Luka took coaching into his own hands 😳 — NBA on ESPN (@ESPNNBA) November 15, 2026 NBA fans saw this unusual moment on social media and flooded it with mixed reactions to Luka Doncic taking over from the coaches to close out tonight’s win. Some appreciated his leadership initiative, while others saw it as a sign of disrespect. “Don’t complain. People have been wanting Luka to show leadership of ‘his’ team, so here you go.” “Luka said, ‘Forget the coach, I’ve got this.’ 😭😂” “I don’t like him snatching that out of her hands.” “His team blew a 31-point lead; I don’t blame him.” “You can do this when you’re a court assassin like him.” “Even Kobe wasn’t this disrespectful… lol.” Several similar reactions flooded social media as the Lakers eventually held on to the lead and won by eight points. After the game, the Lakers’ media asked Luka Doncic about the incident at the press conference. “That stays between the team, man. That’ll stay with the team; they know what I was communicating,” Doncic said as he refused to reveal the details of the incident. So it remains unknown why Luka Doncic did this down the stretch, but it clearly shows he knows that even when defense isn’t his primary responsibility, the leadership onus is on him to rally the troops. In my opinion, this is not a sign of disrespect. Even LeBron James has done something similar to this in the past when he was the face of the Lakers. The team has improved to 12-2 and extended their winning streak to eight games, with Luka Doncic dropping MVP-caliber performances every other night. He is currently averaging 39.0 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 7.8 assists while shooting 48.6% from the field and 40.6% from beyond the arc. The Lakers now move to face the Hornets at Los Angeles’ Crypto.com Arena on Tuesday night, November 17. It remains to be seen how long this winning streak lasts with Doncic in such fiery form and leading the Lakers from the front.

item.title: Taylor Swift Skips Chiefs Game as Travis Kelce’s Injury Raises New Concerns
item.description: Taylor Swift Falcons Game Getty Taylor Swift was absent from the Kansas City Chiefs‘ game against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, November 15, as her husband, Travis Kelce, briefly left the game with an ankle injury. The Chiefs tight end suffered the injury on his first reception of the game when Falcons safety DeMarcco Hellams tackled him following a 23-yard catch-and-run. The Chiefs initially listed Kelce as questionable to return, but he reentered the game with 7:05 remaining in the second quarter. Travis Kelce Returns After Ankle Injury Against Atlanta Falcons Travis Kelce #chiefs Left leg/ankle gets rolled up on. Being evaluated on the sideline pic.twitter.com/Sa7Z5icOqw — Tom Christ, PT, DPT, OCS, FAAOMPT (@FantasyInjuryT) November 15, 2026 Kelce’s injury occurred during Kansas City’s opening offensive possession. After catching a pass from Patrick Mahomes , Kelce gained 23 yards before Hellams brought him down. The defender appeared to pull and roll onto Kelce’s ankle as he completed the tackle. Kelce appeared upset after Hellams rolled onto his ankle during the tackle. The 37-year-old got up slowly and limped toward the sideline before eventually heading to the locker room with members of Kansas City’s training staff. He did not return during the remainder of the Chiefs’ opening drive, which ended with Mahomes throwing a touchdown pass to running back Emmett Johnson. That catch extended his streak to 200 consecutive games with at least one reception. Taylor Swift Has Avoided Chiefs Road Games This Season Andy Reid says TE Jared Wiley fractured his ankle. RG Trey Smith is in the concussion protocol. TE Travis Kelce (ankle) returned to the game, as did C Creed Humphrey, who got poked in the eye. CB Mansoor Delane landed on his back. Reid said it looks like it scared him but not… — Matt Derrick (@mattderrick) November 15, 2026 Swift’s absence in Atlanta follows her attendance pattern throughout the 2026 NFL season. Since officially becoming Mrs. Kelce , Swift has been a constant presence in his suite at Arrowhead Stadium, but has not been spotted at the team’s road games. She also skipped every Chiefs away game last season, with security concerns reportedly contributing to her decision. Swift has taken a more private approach to attending games in Kansas City, frequently entering the stadium without being photographed. She has also appeared less frequently during television broadcasts than she did during Kelce’s 2023 and 2024 seasons. item.title: TRADE: Milwaukee Brewers Acquire 30-Year-Old Pitcher From San Francisco Giants
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 23: Manager Pat Murphy of the Milwaukee Brewers speaks to media at a press conference prior to game one of the 2026 World Series at American Family Field on October 23, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) Getty PHOENIX, ARIZONA - JULY 01: Manager Tony Vitello #23 gestures towards the bullpen as relief pitcher Ryan Walker #74 of the San Francisco Giants walks off the field during a pitching change in the eighth inning against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field on July 01, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona. (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) Getty The Milwaukee Brewers announced on Sunday that they acquired 30-year-old right-handed reliever Ryan Walker in a trade with the San Francisco Giants. Via the Brewers on X: “We have acquired RHP Ryan Walker from SF in exchange for Minor Leaguers Blake Holub and Gavin Perry. Welcome, Ryan!” We have acquired RHP Ryan Walker from SF in exchange for Minor Leaguers Blake Holub and Gavin Perry Welcome, Ryan! pic.twitter.com/lzVJwofNHj — Milwaukee Brewers (@Brewers) November 15, 2026 Milwaukee Brewers Trade 2 Minor Leaguers to San Francisco Giants For RHP Ryan Walker Getty PHOENIX, ARIZONA – JULY 01: Manager Tony Vitello #23 gestures towards the bullpen as relief pitcher Ryan Walker #74 of the San Francisco Giants walks off the field during a pitching change in the eighth inning against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field on July 01, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona. (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) Walker has four years of big-league experience, all with the Giants. He is coming off a rough 2026 season, posting a 7.16 ERA with 23 strikeouts and 19 walks over 32 2/3 innings. More to come. item.title: Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza states the obvious about his tough start vs. Seahawks
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza states the obvious about his tough start vs. Seahawks appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Fernando Mendoza made the first start of his NFL career against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 10, and it did not go great. The rookie Las Vegas Raiders quarterback got on the board early with a rushing touchdown , but he struggled in the passing game (17-of-29, 143 yards, no touchdowns) as the Raiders fell, 21-13. The No. 1 overall pick in this year’s draft acknowledges that his challenging performance against the reigning Super Bowl champions is the first step in a long learning process for him as an NFL quarterback . “There’s a lot of things I need to improve on out on that field,” Mendoza said, per Jesse Merrick. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) One such area of improvement Mendoza cited is his pocket presence, stating that he needs to be “more composed.” Mendoza was sacked six times by the Seahawks in his debut start, which was not entirely on the Raiders’ offensive line. The team’s previous starter, Kirk Cousins, had been sacked just 11 times in his nine starts for Las Vegas this season. Mendoza must do a better job of feeling the pressure inside the pocket, when to scramble, and when to throw balls away. That will usually come with more experience. However, the Raiders could also stand to help out their rookie quarterback by giving him a more reliable offensive weapons. The Raiders’ RB tandem of Mike Washington Jr. and Ashton Jeanty had a disappointing performance, combining for just 41 yards on 17 carries. Meanwhile, tight end Brock Bowers left the game early due to an ankle injury , further limiting Mendoza’s receiving options. Mendoza and the Raiders will look to make some improvements next week, when they take on the Denver Broncos fresh off their bye week. Related: Raiders’ Fernando Mendoza shares positive takeaway from brutal first NFL start Related: Raiders’ Klint Kubiak gives clear verdict of Fernando Mendoza’s first NFL start

item.title: 'Time is running out.' How Texans fumbled a golden opportunity to get back into the playoff race.
item.description: Emari Demercado, Tank Dell and the Texans' offense struggled mightily after jumping out to a 17-point lead and departed Cleveland with a crushing loss to the Browns that could be a significant hit to their playof hopes. (Brett Coomer/Houston Chronicle) CLEVELAND - The Houston Texans held a 3-point lead with 5:19 remaining when safety Calen Bullock intercepted Clevleand Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson at Houston's 23-yard-line. It should have been a moment of victory for the Texans, who for one half, played better than the Browns. The Texans should have been able to run out the clock on offense. On defense, they should have been able to stop the Browns. But things have rarely gone as planned for the Texans this season. They lost to their own former franchise quarterback Watson and the Browns 27-24, falling to 3-6 on Sunday at Huntington Bank Field. And again, the Texans allowed another team to score a game-winning touchdown against them in the game's final minutes. If this sounds like a broken record, it's because it is one. Texans Insider with Jonathan M. Alexander Sign up for an in-depth newsletter with Houston Texans news, features and predictions. The Texans are the only team in the past 50 seasons to lose five times within their first nine games when tied or leading in the final two minutes. "It goes back to the fact that we can't hurt ourselves," coach DeMeco Ryans said. "When you have 13 penalties, especially there late in the game - we need to move the football, and we get penalties on special teams, penalties offensively, penalties on defense. All three phases had critical penalties that hurt us." Those penalties accounted for 112 yards, all of which helped the Browns. That was the story of Sunday's game. Whether it was an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty during a touchdown celebration called against wide receiver Nico Collins, an encroachment penalty on third-and-2 against edge rusher Will Anderson Jr., multiple false starts by left tackle Aireontae Ersery to start drives, or a holding penalty on special teams called against defensive back Kamari Ramsey before the final drive, the Texans just couldn't get out of their own way. It was the Texans who lost this game, and not so much the Browns winning it. "The time is now," quarterback C.J. Stroud said of getting things fixed. "We gotta be more urgent because time is running out." Time is running out. And this loss may have cost the Texans their best shot at getting back into the hunt for a playoff spot. (Brett Coomer/Houston Chronicle) Had the Texans won Sunday, not only would they have owned the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Browns, but they would have been a half-game behind the Browns and the Patriots for the AFC's seventh and final wild card spot. Now, they're 2 ½
