(Brett Coomer/Houston Chronicle) CLEVELAND - The Houston Texans held a 3-point lead with 5:19 remaining when safety Calen Bullock intercepted Clevleand Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson at Houston's 23-yard-line. It should have been a moment of victory for the Texans, who for one half, played better than the Browns. The Texans should have been able to run out the clock on offense. On defense, they should have been able to stop the Browns. But things have rarely gone as planned for the Texans this season. They lost to their own former franchise quarterback Watson and the Browns 27-24, falling to 3-6 on Sunday at Huntington Bank Field. And again, the Texans allowed another team to score a game-winning touchdown against them in the game's final minutes. If this sounds like a broken record, it's because it is one. Texans Insider with Jonathan M. Alexander Sign up for an in-depth newsletter with Houston Texans news, features and predictions. The Texans are the only team in the past 50 seasons to lose five times within their first nine games when tied or leading in the final two minutes. "It goes back to the fact that we can't hurt ourselves," coach DeMeco Ryans said. "When you have 13 penalties, especially there late in the game - we need to move the football, and we get penalties on special teams, penalties offensively, penalties on defense. All three phases had critical penalties that hurt us." Those penalties accounted for 112 yards, all of which helped the Browns. That was the story of Sunday's game. Whether it was an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty during a touchdown celebration called against wide receiver Nico Collins, an encroachment penalty on third-and-2 against edge rusher Will Anderson Jr., multiple false starts by left tackle Aireontae Ersery to start drives, or a holding penalty on special teams called against defensive back Kamari Ramsey before the final drive, the Texans just couldn't get out of their own way. It was the Texans who lost this game, and not so much the Browns winning it. "The time is now," quarterback C.J. Stroud said of getting things fixed. "We gotta be more urgent because time is running out." Time is running out. And this loss may have cost the Texans their best shot at getting back into the hunt for a playoff spot. Houston Texans wide receiver Xavier Hutchinson (19) loses the handle on a pass broken up by Cleveland Browns cornerback Denzel Ward (21) during the second half of an NFL football game in Cleveland, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. (Brett Coomer/Houston Chronicle) Had the Texans won Sunday, not only would they have owned the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Browns, but they would have been a half-game behind the Browns and the Patriots for the AFC's seventh and final wild card spot. Now, they're 2 ½ games behind the Browns, which is more like three because the Browns have the tiebreaker. "Exactly, we ain't got no more time, we ain't got no more excuses, we can't keep losing," Bullock said. "Like (Stroud) said, the time is now but it's running out so we got to come out with wins especially in environments like this, we're going to be back in this position one of these weeks." Perhaps the biggest and most controversial play happened on the Browns' game-winning drive. Cleveland, trailing 24-20, needed a touchdown to take the lead. The Browns had second-and-11 from the 50-yard line with 1:18 remaining when Watson threw a pass to wide receiver Tylan Wallace that ended up in an incompletion and a personal foul penalty on Kamari Lassiter. The officials said Lassiter hit Wallace, who was a defenseless receiver. Further review of the play showed Lassiter trying to make a play on the ball before inadvertently colliding with Wallace - their helmets clashing. Lassiter said he asked the officials for an explanation but got none. "It's very frustrating," Lassiter said after the game. "As a player, it leaves you with a lot of indecision, like what am I supposed to do? Am I supposed to let him catch it? The ball was in the air. I was trying to make a play on the ball." The play proved critical. Instead of third-and-11 from midfield, the Browns had first-and-10 from the Houston 35. But even with that play, the Texans had several opportunities to close it. One play after that penalty, Watson found tight end Harold Fannin Jr. for a 30-yard catch and run. On the next play, with 57 seconds left, Browns running back Quinshon Judkins ran it in for a 5-yard TD that looked so easy it was hard to tell if the Texans hadn't just let him score to get the ball back. Ryans, unfortunately, said that wasn't the intention. "Yeah, we're trying to stop them right there," Ryans said of the TD. "We have to play better - run defense, have to tackle better. We have to stop better, play better, run defense, get a stop." Houston's offense was just as much at fault. It got the ball with 57 seconds left and two timeouts - more than enough time to kick a field goal and tie it. However, nothing was working. Of the seven plays Houston ran on its final drive, Stroud completed only two of those passes. One of those competitions was a first-down pass to Collins, which was negated because of a holding penalty against rookie left guard Febechi Nwaiwu, who was starting in place of the injured Keylan Rutledge. item.title: #13 St. Johns 79, Syracuse 62: tough second half derails Orange in Madison Square Garden
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 15: Kiyan Anthony #7 of the Syracuse Orange looks on during the first half against the St. John's Red Storm at Madison Square Garden on November 15, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images NEW YORK — For the first time since 2015, Sunday night showcased Syracuse and St. John’s facing off at Madison Square Garden in New York City, and after a promising start for the Orange, at the end of the day this matchup showed there are still some growing pains that Coach McNamara’s squad need to fight through. Especially against a nationally ranked opponent as St. John’s outscored Syracuse 49-29 in the second half in route to a 79-62 victory. But while it feels crazy that the two in-state rivals have not played in “World’s Most Famous Arena” in so long, it is safe to say the game lived up to the hype right from the jump. With a Garden at least 60% filled with fans in dressed in Orange, those rooting for the ’Cuse all erupted early. Ryan Moesch got a mismatch on a pick and roll with center Rueben Prey guarding him. And safe to say he took advantage, breaking the junior’s ankles and burying a wide open triple to give Syracuse an 8-6 lead at the first media timeout. But the real story of the first half was Kiyan Anthony. It was the sophomore’s first game at MSG, and he came off the bench leading the Orange with 10 points, getting to the charity stripe on three and-1 opportunities and converting on two of them. Crazy enough, Kiyan one of the main reasons Syracuse took a 33-30 lead into halftime against the naiton’s 13th ranked team. But for the second consecutive game, Syracuse came out flat in the second half, surrendering an 16-2 run to their opponent and quickly giving up the lead they worked so hard to earn in the first 20 minutes. All of a sudden it was 46-35 Red Storm before you could even blink. Until a bit of a response off the bench from Amari Monroe, who went on a quick 5-0 run on his own and cut the deficit to six at 46-40. However, the Pitino press was grueling, and suffocated the Orange right when you thought they might get back into the game. Syracuse could not buy a basket in the second half, shooting 33% from the field and only scoring a mere 29 points. The Orange showed a bit of fight late, but they could never make the big shot to really make the Red Storm feel any pressure while also turning the ball over at very inopportune times.

item.title: Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake field hockey falls to Lakeland in double overtime of state final
item.description: Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake freshman Taylor Loria moves the ball for Burnt Hills during Sunday's Class B state championship game at Arlington High School in LaGrangeville. (Kyle Adams/For the Times Union) LAGRANGEVILLE - Winning a state championship is extremely difficult to do. The Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake field hockey team was reminded of that on Sunday afternoon, as the Spartans came up just short of winning the program's third consecutive state title. Burnt Hills dropped a 1-0 game in double overtime, as Section 1's Lakeland won the NYSPHSAA Class B championship. Lakeland (21-2-1 overall) standout Gianna Santini, a UMass Lowell field hockey commit, finally found the back of the cage as she converted on a penalty corner for the Hornets early in the second overtime period. "Sharon Sarsen is a phenomenal coach and has a phenomenal program," Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake head coach Kelly Vrooman said of Lakeland. "She's been there for years and they're a well-oiled machine. I knew this coming into it, and our girls didn't take them lightly. We both have young teams and I just think we fell a little short." Lakeland's win at Arlington High School gave the program its 14th state title, which have all come under Sarsen, with the first coming in 1990. Burnt Hills and Lakeland both had chances to score on Sunday and evenly shared time of possession. The Spartans tallied eight penalty corners, while the Hornets had six. "They had plenty of opportunities and we had plenty of opportunities," Vrooman said. "We had corners and they had corners, but it could have gone either way at any time." The Spartans' best opportunity was likely as time expired in the first half. Burnt Hills was awarded back-to-back corners, but was unable to score. "They play a totally different style of field hockey than we do. This one game isn't going to define us, but they got the best of us this time," said Burnt Hills senior goalie Isabella Yecies. "This game wasn't easy. We want to play the best competition that we can, games that will be challenging for us. We just came up a little short." Burnt Hills, which ended its season with a record of 16-3-1, topped Section 5's Pittsford-Sutherland 5-0 on Saturday to reach Sunday's state final. "We weren't the same team that we were yesterday, and that made a difference," Vrooman said. "We always just tell ourselves, we have to recommit. After this game, we'll take a breath, regroup and recommit to our mission. It's never really a goal to get here, but the fact that we did this year is a delight. "We have a very young team and I'm really proud that we got this far. We could have made history, but it didn't happen this year - and that's OK. We're not going to let this game define who we are as a program." Burnt Hills defeated South Glens Falls 6-1 on Nov. 1 to win its fourth consecutive Section 2 title, its 13th in the last 15 years. Burnt Hills dropped a 1-0 game in double overtime, as Section 1's Lakeland won the NYSPHSAA Class B championship. Lakeland (21-2-1 overall) standout Gianna Santini, a UMass Lowell field hockey commit, finally found the back of the cage as she converted on a penalty corner for the Hornets early in the second overtime period. "Sharon Sarsen is a phenomenal coach and has a phenomenal program," Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake head coach Kelly Vrooman said of Lakeland. "She's been there for years and they're a well-oiled machine. "This game wasn't easy. We want to play the best competition that we can, games that will be challenging for us. We just came up a little short." Burnt Hills, which ended its season with a record of 16-3-1, topped Section 5's Pittsford-Sutherland 5-0 on Saturday to reach Sunday's state final. We're not going to let this game define who we are as a program." Burnt Hills defeated South Glens Falls 6-1 on Nov. 1 to win its fourth consecutive Section 2 title, its 13th in the last 15 years. It won the regional title on Nov. 8 with a 5-0 victory over Section 3's New Hartford. The Spartans won their first state title in Class A in 1987, when Vrooman was a player. Burnt Hills won the 2021, 2024 and 2025 Class B state championships, all with Vrooman as coach. Burnt Hills' 2024 state championship completed a perfect season with a 3-0 victory over Lakeland. Burnt Hills will say goodbye to seven seniors, including captains Grace Kogut, Katie Lansley and Yecies. Kogut and Lansley have been on the team since they were eighth graders. "Just like every year, with every senior that leaves, (we'll miss) the leadership, the level of intensity and passing along the tradition," Vrooman said. "Someone is going to step up. They always do." Subscribe There’s more to Albany with the Times Union. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Jimmy Connors shares skin cancer diagnosis
item.description: 74-year-old American tennis legend Jimmy Connors, winner of a record-setting 109 ATP titles, recently shared a health update that is not uncommon to athletes who play outdoor sports. Connors revealed at the beginning of a recent episode of his “Advantage Connors” podcast he hosts with his son Brett that he was diagnosed with skin cancer on his ear. MORE: Where is former ATP World No. 1 Jimmy Connors? Though Connors did not specify what type of skin cancer it was: basal cell, squamous cell, or melanoma, he did share that he is six weeks into his treatment. Part of Connors’ ear was bandaged. He promised to show viewers the “finished product” when his ear is fully recovered. This news came as a surprise because Connors looked healthy at the US Open in September. Jimbo! Pleasure to have you today, Jimmy Connors 🫡🇺🇸 https://t.co/nsLlo22Rdv — US Open Tennis (@usopen) September 13, 2026 What Connors said Jul 2, 2977; London, ENGLAND; FILE PHOTO; Jimmy Connors (USA) returns a shot during the 1977 Wimbledon Championships at the All England Lawn Tennis Club. Mandatory Credit: Gerry Cranham/Offside Sports via USA TODAY Sports Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Connors encouraged people to wear sunscreen. He is undergoing multiple surgeries to rebuild his ear. He commended his medical team which is taking good care of him but urged people to protect themselves from the sun so they do not have to go through this. Connors is a living legend who has remained close to the game through coaching, broadcasting, and now podcasting since retiring in 1996. He won eight Grand Slams and was the ATP World No. 1 in 1974. Connors was one of the biggest showmen and greatest American men to ever play the game. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: 4 Things We Learned From Mavericks’ 37-Point Blowout Loss Against Celtics
item.description: Nov 15, 2026; Boston, Massachusetts, USA; Dallas Mavericks forward Cooper Flagg (32) drives past Boston Celtics forward Jayson Tatum (0) during the first quarter at TD Garden. Mandatory Credit: Winslow Townson-Imagn Images On paper, the Dallas Mavericks have an immensely promising roster. Led by the star duo of Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving , the Mavericks boast the potential to be an immensely competitive team in the West. Unfortunately, this wasn’t the case on Sunday night. In a game against the Boston Celtics on the road, Dallas’ status as a young team was put on full display, as the Celtics handed the Mavericks a blowout 131-94 loss. For the most part, Dallas was just outmatched, as Jayson Tatum led the Celtics’ charge with 32 points, six rebounds, and six assists in 30 minutes of action. Given that no player on the Mavericks’ roster scored over 20 points, the difference in quality was apparent. While Dallas’ shorthanded rotation with Kyrie Irving sidelined may have been to blame for the team’s poor performances, several other factors played a role. On that note, we examine four things we learned from the Mavs’ outing against the Celtics on Sunday. The Mavericks’ First-Quarter Defense Needs Work The first thing that stood out from Sunday night’s game was the Mavericks’ poor defensive effort in the first quarter. Aside from their abysmal offensive production, scoring only nine points to start the game, the Mavs allowed Boston to score 42 points, offering virtually no resistance against one of the best teams in the league. For obvious reasons, this is disappointing. But when observing recent trends , it becomes far more concerning. Over the Mavericks’ last four matchups (including Sunday), Dallas has allowed the opposing team to score 30+ in the first quarter of each game. Although the Mavs have held their own offensively in almost every outing to limit the gap, their 1-3 record during this period doesn’t inspire much confidence. As things stand, the Mavs post a defensive rating of 112.8 (before Sunday’s game), which ranks 13th in the NBA. However, when focusing solely on the first quarter, their defensive rating of 111.1 sees them ranked 20th in the league. Needless to say, this may be worth addressing. Cooper Flagg Has Room To Grow A key factor that stood out on Sunday night was Cooper Flagg’s performance. Against the Celtics, the Maine native was in a familiar environment, and in Kyrie Irving’s absence, Flagg was the sole superstar on the floor for Dallas. In such a situation, the 19-year-old faced some challenges. Cooper Flagg ended the night with 17 points, three rebounds, four assists, a steal, and a block. In isolation, these seem like solid figures. However, when factoring in his status as the focal point on offense, along with his shooting splits of 5-15 FG and 2-6 3PT FG, Flagg’s limitations were made apparent. In all fairness, the 19-year-old’s potential is mesmerizing . Some of the shots he made against Boston reflected this aspect

However, when focusing solely on the first quarter, their defensive rating of 111.1 sees them ranked 20th in the league. Needless to say, this may be worth addressing. Cooper Flagg Has Room To Grow A key factor that stood out on Sunday night was Cooper Flagg’s performance. Against the Celtics, the Maine native was in a familiar environment, and in Kyrie Irving’s absence, Flagg was the sole superstar on the floor for Dallas. In such a situation, the 19-year-old faced some challenges. Cooper Flagg ended the night with 17 points, three rebounds, four assists, a steal, and a block. In isolation, these seem like solid figures. However, when factoring in his status as the focal point on offense, along with his shooting splits of 5-15 FG and 2-6 3PT FG, Flagg’s limitations were made apparent. In all fairness, the 19-year-old’s potential is mesmerizing . Some of the shots he made against Boston reflected this aspect of his game. However, in Irving’s absence, the forward drew significantly more defensive pressure due to the lack of a secondary scorer. In many ways, this is an obstacle that Flagg will overcome. However, at this juncture, it just highlights that he is far from reaching his true potential. Zaccharie Risacher Seems To Be Fitting In Zaccharie Risacher was one of the more intriguing additions the Mavericks made to their roster this offseason. After trading for the former first-round pick, many doubted how Risacher would fit into Dallas’ rotation, especially in light of his struggles with the Hawks last season. For the most part, Sunday night’s game answered those doubts. Zaccharie Risacher led the Mavericks in scoring with 18 points, adding five rebounds on an efficient 8-9 shooting from the field to go with it in 27 minutes of action. Although he ended the game with a +/- rating of -14, one could safely say that he was one of the better players for Dallas. In all fairness, it is hard to say Risacher was impactful simply because of how the Celtics put the game away in the first half itself. Still, with a quick six points in the second quarter and another seven points in the third, the former first-round pick helped Dallas stabilize their offense, ensuring that they remained marginally competitive for the remainder of the game. This season, Risacher is averaging 8.1 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 1.3 steals per game while shooting 42.4% from the field. Although his production seems to be down compared to last season, the 21-year-old is gradually adapting to his new role in Dallas. Dallas Desperately Needs Dereck Lively II Back Aside from all the factors that stood out from Sunday night’s game, the most important one was probably the need for a stronger interior presence. While Dallas typically benefits from a strong big man rotation featuring Daniel Gafford and Moussa Cisse , Dereck Lively II’s absence was telling against the Celtics. Dallas’ centers were completely outmatched against Boston. Gafford, who has cultivated a reputation for being a phenomenal blue-collar big man, posted only three points and four rebounds against the Celtics. Off the bench, Cisse, who gave the Mavericks much to be optimistic about last season, had virtually no opportunities to contribute, notching only one point and a rebound in four minutes of playing time. With the Celtics beating the Mavericks on the rebounding glass 52-38 and also outscoring them 36-32 in the paint, Dallas clearly needs a stronger presence on the inside. In this regard, the Mavericks can only hope Dereck Lively II returns to action soon. Given the 22-year-old’s rebounding and elite rim protection ability, Dallas would benefit greatly from having another reliable center in their frontcourt rotation.

item.title: Evan McPherson's Bengals-record field-goal streak ends at 25
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals kicker Evan McPherson's team-record streak of consecutive field goals made ended at 25, with a miss on a 43-yard attempt during the second quarter of the team's NFL Week 10 showdown with the Pittsburgh Steelers on NBC's Sunday Night Football at Paycor Stadium. It was McPherson's first field-goal miss of the season. McPherson made a 24-yarder in the first quarter. McPherson made a pair of field goals, including one from 57 yards, during the Bengals' NFL Week 9 win against the Atlanta Falcons at Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain. McPherson made a 26-yard field goal to break the franchise record for most consecutive field goals converted with 22, during the fourth quarter of the team's NFL Week 5 win against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. McPherson's streak dated back to Week 11 of the 2025 season. He broke the record held by Shayne Graham, who made 21 consecutive FGs in 2007. McPherson was named AFC Special Teams Player of the Month for September. McPherson converted each of his eight field-goal attempts and eight extra points over the Bengals' three games in September. McPherson 's 32 points scored in September tied for the most by any NFL kicker, while his FG total tied for the most by an AFC kicker. McPherson also led all kickers in FGs made from 50 or more yards (five). McPherson is in his sixth NFL season, all with the Bengals. In 2025, McPherson broke his own record for longest field goal in team history with a 63-yarder to end the first half of the Week 12 loss to New England at Paycor Stadium. McPherson's kick was one of 14 field goals in NFL history of at least 63 yards. McPherson attempted a 67-yard field goal at the end of the first half of the team's NFL Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. He made the attempt , but it didn't count. The Packers called timeout, and the whistle blew to negate what would have been an NFL record. McPherson played in 12 games during the 2024 season , missing time because of a groin injury. This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: Evan McPherson's Bengals-record field-goal streak ends at 25

item.description: Here's everything Houston Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said following Week 10's 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns , including the issues in the second half, plans for a change of direction next week and an injury update on running back Woody Marks. DeMeco Ryans Opening statement: “First and foremost, all honor and glory to our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. Credit to the Browns for finding a way to finish the football game and win. A really talented football team and they found a way to win it. For us, we didn’t do a great job there of playing clean. Way too many penalties there late in the game; didn’t execute properly. Too many penalties - hurt ourselves and found ourselves on the losing end of this game. We have to find a way to look at it, flush it, get better, and move on to Thursday night.” Question: What do you make of the way you went up 17 and then gave up those points? Ryans: “It goes back to we can’t hurt ourselves. When you have 13 penalties, especially there late in the game - we need to move the football, and we get penalties on special teams, penalties offensively, penalties on defense. All three phases had critical penalties that hurt us.” Q: When it comes to that one penalty, the one where Texans CB Kamari Lassiter was flagged - what did you see on the play? What is your understanding of the rule? Ryans: “I saw Kamari going up for the football. Nothing was intentional there by Kamari. He is going up for thefootball. I have to look at it and see how that is a penalty on him.” Q: There were six possessions that you all had on offense after you scored your last points. You had five punts and one interception. What changed? Ryans: “It wasn't good offensively coming out in the second half. We started really fast, but they applied pressure on us - a ton of pressure there in the second half, and we didn't make plays in the second half. We didn't move thefootball in the third quarter. Ryans: “It's all-encompassing. Run game, passing game. We have to do a better job at all of it.” Q: Another late game, but the defense at the end - you all went up. They needed a touchdown score. You all gave up a touchdown. How do you all fix that going into Thursday night? Ryans: “I have to call it better. We have to find a way to adjust things quicker and be able to move the ball, scorepoints.” Q: How much do you think the ineffectiveness of the run game factored into the offense not being able to move the ball the way that you would like? Ryans: “It's all-encompassing. Run game, passing game. We have to do a better job at all of it.” Q: Another late game, but the defense at the end - you all went up. They needed a touchdown score. You all gave up a touchdown. How do you all fix that going into Thursday night? Ryans: “I have to call it better. I'll look at it, look at myself, how can I call it better and put the guys in a better position to make a play?” Q: The picture is 3-6. This was one you obviously had to have. How do you look at the season's perspective right now? Ryans: “To me, everyone is one you have to have. That's how I look at it and right now it wasn't good enough. Credit to the Browns, they found a way to win it today.” Q: Does this feel like a missed opportunity here? Ryans: “We lost the game.” Q: That last score, were you trying to get the ball back? Were you trying to let them score or were you trying to stop them? Ryans: “Yeah, we're trying to stop them right there. We have to play better - run defense, have to tackle better. We have to stop better, play better, run defense, be stopped there, get a stop.” Q: What went into not being able to contain Browns QB Deshaun Watson and keep him in the pocket? He got a lot of yards outside the pocket. Ryans: "Deshaun got a lot of yards, especially on the one play earlier in the game where he scrambled outside on us, we're in man coverage. Everybody's eyes are on their man, and he got out of the pocket on us. So he made acouple plays.” Q: Did they make an adjustment? It looked like early on, Texans WR Nico Collins was having his way with their defense, but then the percentages started to go down. Ryans: “They did a good job of making plays, and when the ball was up, they did a good job of making plays on the football. They brought more pressure in the second half, and we couldn't get drives going.” Q: You mentioned needing to call it better. In what ways did you feel like you could have called it better? Ryans: “I just have to put guys in better positions. When you come out and you score that many points in the second half, we have to do a better job of getting stops there.” Q: Obviously, the defense started well. What do you think kind of changed? Ryans: “They got the ball out quick. They hit an explosive on us earlier in the game. They hit an explosive. We could be better there with how we play it. Overall, they started to get the ball out quicker and make some plays. Deshaun made some plays running around on the edge. But the game, to me, it really came down to the penalties. Thirteen penalties. Then it came down to third down. We only converted like three third downs, and they were 7-15. So some of those third and medium plays that they were able to convert and stay on the field, we did get stops. Then vice versa, our offense didn't convert enough third downs to stay on the field and really get drivessustained and keep the ball moving. So that's where the game kind of tilted in their favor.” Q: We've talked about penalties most of the season. Do you think that’s a common theme with you guys? Like sometimes it'll get better and then it keeps coming up. Ryans: “We’ll have to look at it again. I thought we were much better last week with the penalties and now it shows up again this week. It's just some inconsistencies there. We have to take a deep dive and see how we can getbetter.” Q: It seemed like Texans QB C.J. Stroud started off hot and kind of cooled off. How would you assess overall? Ryans: “I thought C.J. still made some plays, right? Even with the pressure that was on him, I thought he was still able to move around in the pocket and scramble and run to get first down a couple of times. Then he kept plays alive. He was under a lot of pressure. He didn't take a lot of sacks, so I'm still happy with how he played, happy withthe decisions that he was able to make.” Q: Quick turnaround. How do you get this fixed before Thursday night? Ryans: “Hey, you gotta move on quickly. You can't dwell on this. The issues that we have, we look at it. Everybody looks at themselves first and sees where we can be better. We move on; got a good team coming in on Thursday night.” Q: We haven't talked since Wednesday and Thursday's practice. Texans DE Danielle Hunter and Texans DE WillAnderson, Jr. popped up on the injury report. What happened? Ryans: “Danielle had a hamstring injury, and Will just had an ankle injury, and he was fine.” Q: What is the prognosis on Texans RB Woody Marks? Ryans: “Woody was diagnosed with a concussion, so he'll be in concussion protocol. We probably won't have him for Thursday night. It's not enough time for him to turn it around.” Q: Do you think Texans RB David Montgomery, now that he had a brief ramp-up week might possibly play? Ryans: “I'm not certain if David can play or not. We'll see how he is when we get back.” Q: With Danielle, do you think it’s short-term or do you think it’s a longer-term thing? Ryans: “We’ll take it one day at a time to see how he feels and how he can get back.” Q: You guys haven't been a good finishing team all year and having lost this game in this manner, does that concern you? Ryans: “We’ve got to play better.” Q: So it doesn't concern you? Ryans: “Anytime you lose; any time, for me - we pour everything into this, right? So does it concern [me]? Everything we do, all the time we spend, everything that we do is geared toward finding a way to win football games. All right? And when you don't win, and you come up short, you go back to the drawing board. You try to find a way to correct it, move forward, and make the necessary changes you need, right? But I'm not discouraged at all. We stick together, we keep moving forward.” Q: Is the amount of penalties coming from being undisciplined or is that just not trus

item.title: Rams make history with absurd Ronnie Rivers spamming to finish off the Cardinals
item.description: Arianna Grainey-Imagn Images Rams make history with absurd Ronnie Rivers spamming to finish off the Cardinals appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Rams leaned heavily into Puka Nacua and Matthew Stafford in the past. But LA and Sean McVay turned to a surprise option to wear down the Arizona Cardinals: Ronnie Rivers. The undrafted running back out of Fresno State stole the spotlight late in the 34-6 rout down in Glendale, Arizona. And LA made history in the process with Rivers, per ESPN Insights after the game . “The Rams ended their victory with a 17-play drive that took the final 12:15 of the game. The first 15 plays were all carries by Ronnie Rivers. Rivers is the first player with 15+ touches on a single drive over the last 25 seasons, previous most in that span was 13,” the account posted on X, formerly known as Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Rivers’ best run became a 16-yarder. He also delivered an 11-yard scamper during that drive. But he emerged as the stunning third trusted backfield option on a team featuring two backfield stars. Ram fans are used to Kyren Williams wearing down defenses and becoming a Pro Bowler in the process. But Williams settled for 12 carries for 23 yards and averaged 1.9 yards a carry. Blake Corum pummeled Arizona the most, racking up 17 carries for 100 yards. Rivers, though, handed the Rams 81 rushing yards which becomes a career-high for him. He averaged 5.4 yards per carry in the desert. Los Angeles once landed him after the 2022 NFL Draft, but he never began his career with the Rams. Arizona rose as his first NFL employer, taking him after that draft class. So Sunday became long-awaited closet revenge on the first team that released him. And he pulled it off amid injuries to Nacua and Rivers’ fellow Fresno State grad Davante Adams . Related: Rams Week 10 injury report vs. Cardinals: Puka Nacua is on IR, so who will step up for LA? Related: Rams’ biggest mistake at 2026 NFL Trade Deadline

item.title: Dolphins vs. Bills odds: Opening lines for Week 11 matchup
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 15: Kyle McCord #14 of the Miami Dolphins scores a touchdown against Cam Bynum #0 of the Indianapolis Colts during the fourth quarter at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins fell to 1-8 earlier today after coming up just short of beating the Indianapolis Colts, 24-22. Miami’s offense played well enough under quarterback Kyle McCord, making his NFL debut after spending his rookie season on the Philadelphia Eagles’ practice squad last year, and the defense did its part to keep Miami in the game. The special teams let down the Dolphins – with kicker Zane Gonzalez missing two field goals and an extra point during the game. The Dolphins’ loss was yet another straight-up loss, but they did enough to cover the 3.5-point spread throughout the week, or the 4.5-point mark to which the spread ballooned on Sunday. Miami is being given an even bigger window for next week’s game. Miami visits the Buffalo Bills in Week 11, the first of two meetings between the AFC East rivals in 2026. According to FanDuel Sportsbook, the Dolphins have little chance against the division-leading Bills. The opening line has the Bills favored by 16.5 points . Buffalo demolished the New York Jets, another AFC East division opponent, on Sunday, 31-12. The win moved the Bills to 8-1 for the year and keeps them in the top spot in the AFC playoff picture, a game ahead of the Kansas City Chiefs and Jacksonville Jaguars. The winner of tonight’s Sunday Night Football game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals will also reach the 7-2 mark, a game behind Buffalo. The Bills are -1800 on the moneyline for the straight-up victory, while the Dolphins are +980. The point total opened at 47.5. McCord will start his second game in Week 11, looking to continue to grow in the Dolphins’ offense as he replaces Malik Willis, who is on injured reserve with a groin injury. McCord finished the game 17-for-32 for 209 yards with no touchdown passes or interceptions; he did score a rushing touchdown. The Dolphins and Bills will kickoff at 1 p.m. Eastern on Sunday, November 22. Phins up! Dive into game day on the SB Nation app! Celebrate every score and talk through every twist and turn with fellow Dolphins fans in real time. item.title: David Tennant Officially Returns to Doctor Who in 2027
item.description: The future of Doctor Who is uncertain, but at the very least, the universe has heard the pleas of fans who are in desperate need of more of David Tennant as the Tenth Doctor. That's right, there's even more time and space adventures for Tennant on the way, as he'll be reprising his role in a new audio drama from Big Finish — a British production company known for producing Doctor Who audio dramas and shorts .

item.title: Halo Defined a Generation of LAN Parties — Then It Killed Them
item.description: So old, in fact, that the upcoming 25th anniversary of the Xbox and Halo: Combat Evolved immediately made me think about the LAN parties my brother and I used to host in middle and high school. There were a dozen or so teenage boys, four TVs, and enough Ethernet cable to turn my parents’ house into a tripping hazard that could also burst into flames at any moment. I’ve played countless multiplayer games since, but none have come close to the majesty of those experiences.

item.title: Apple’s new study looks to improve the effectiveness of AI health tools
item.description: Apple announced a new study today with the goal of better understanding how people interact with conversational AI health tools and how useful their responses actually are. The company is conducting the Apple Health AI Usage Study in collaboration with OpenEvidence , a clinical AI platform used by healthcare professionals that generates answers based on medical information from sources like The New England Journal of Medicine . Participants will use a new iOS app to ask medical questions and then rate the responses based on criteria including accuracy, detail, and relevance. The app is now available for download, and enrollment starts today, … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Three Lions’ win over Spain comes in two acts: the first superb, the second heroic | Sid Lowe
item.description: Visitors take game to world champions and, though their hold on possession plummets, their rearguard is outstanding In the final, absurdly tense moments before England finally did it and Spain finally fell, when Dan Burn had been sent on to do Dan Burn things, when the board had gone up with a 4 on but the clock wasn’t moving fast enough and the men in red kept coming back, Harry Kane had come to the side of the pitch to stand beside Thomas Tuchel. Palms out, Kane signalled and directed and appealed with his teammates to hold on to what they had: s omehow, anyhow . What they had was special, but their grip on it was not as secure as it had seemed. Not as secure as it should have been too. Tuchel gave Kane a nudge that looked pretty playful considering the pressure, before Marc Bollengier, the fourth official, ordered him back to the bench. But England’s captain was not gone for long and when he returned he was joined by almost all of them, awaiting the big moment. From there, he watched James Trafford make an astonishing double save, a moment of heroism that allowed them to hang on. Then, standing alongside the rest who could no longer just sit there, he saw the last header clear – Dan Burn things – before the whistle went. Then he and they went on one last run, back on to the pitch. Continue reading...

item.title: Microsoft lifts Indian cloud prices by 15 percent, cuts costs in China
item.description: Microsoft has announced massive price rises for commercial cloud services in India and New Zealand, but a substantial reduction in China. The software giant sells its cloudy services in many local currencies, at an equivalent rate to the prices it charges in the USA. As exchange rates shift, so do the prices Microsoft charges around the world. Microsoft last week announced the new charges that will come into effect from January 1, 2027, and the news isn’t pleasant for customers in India, who face an increase of 15.7 percent for cloud services and up to 20 percent for some on-prem offerings. New Zealand customers face a ten percent price hike. Customers in China, where Microsoft relies on a local partner called 21Vianet to deliver its cloud, will see costs fall by up to 8.5 percent. Australian buyers will see costs fall by 4.5 percent. The only nation not in Asia on Microsoft’s list is Norway, where prices will ease 5.9 percent. Sega Japan hits double trouble Sega has just had a rotten week that saw it battle a data leak and an outage. The outage impacted the company’s ALL.Net and Aime services, which connect arcade games across different locations. The services include administrative features for arcade operators, plus services for gamers including pre-payment to play, high score and profile recording, and networked gaming. Sega suspended some ALL.Net and Aime services on November 1 after discovering unauthorized access to servers. At least thirteen games and services were then unavailable until around November 15. The company hasn’t explained what went wrong, but assured customers the incident was not a data breach and that payment information was safe. But data did leak for those who subscribe to some Sega newsletters. Sega uses a third-party outfit called Arara Co. to send some emails, and it leaked email addresses. No other personal data leaked from Arara. Sega has nonetheless warned newsletter recipients to watch out for suspicious messages. Alibaba floats chip unit Chinese tech giant Alibaba last week announced its intention to float its T-Head chip design biz on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. The filing announcing the spinoff describes T-Head as “a leading provider of full-stack data center chips which enable system-level compute solutions in China,” suggesting Alibaba doesn’t think buyers in the rest of the world are keen to acquire its chips. T-Head going public “allows a more efficient deployment of Alibaba Group’s financial resources,” the filing states, and should also mean the chip design outfit can more easily find third-party customers. item.dc:creator: Simon Sharwood
item.content:encoded: Microsoft has announced massive price rises for commercial cloud services in India and New Zealand, but a substantial reduction in China. The software giant sells its cloudy services in many local currencies, at an equivalent rate to the prices it charges in the USA. As exchange rates shift, so do the prices Microsoft charges around the world. Microsoft last week announced the new charges that will come into effect from January 1, 2027, and the news isn’t pleasant for customers in India, who face an increase of 15.7 percent for cloud services and up to 20 percent for some on-prem offerings. New Zealand customers face a ten percent price hike. Customers in China, where Microsoft relies on a local partner called 21Vianet to deliver its cloud, will see costs fall by up to 8.5 percent. Australian buyers will see costs fall by 4.5 percent. The only nation not in Asia on Microsoft’s list is Norway, where prices will ease 5.9 percent. Sega Japan hits double trouble Sega has just had a rotten week that saw it battle a data leak and an outage. The outage impacted the company’s ALL.Net and Aime services, which connect arcade games across different locations. The services include administrative features for arcade operators, plus services for gamers including pre-payment to play, high score and profile recording, and networked gaming. Sega suspended some ALL.Net and Aime services on November 1 after discovering unauthorized access to servers. At least thirteen games and services were then unavailable until around November 15. The company hasn’t explained what went wrong, but assured customers the incident was not a data breach and that payment information was safe. But data did leak for those who subscribe to some Sega newsletters. Sega uses a third-party outfit called Arara Co. to send some emails, and it leaked email addresses. No other personal data leaked from Arara. Sega has nonetheless warned newsletter recipients to watch out for suspicious messages. Alibaba floats chip unit Chinese tech giant Alibaba last week announced its intention to float its T-Head chip design biz on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. The filing announcing the spinoff describes T-Head as “a leading provider of full-stack data center chips which enable system-level compute solutions in China,” suggesting Alibaba doesn’t think buyers in the rest of the world are keen to acquire its chips. T-Head going public “allows a more efficient deployment of Alibaba Group’s financial resources,” the filing states, and should also mean the chip design outfit can more easily find third-party customers. India bans export of dead batteries The government of India last week banned the export of “Lithium-Ion battery Black Mass” – a powdery substance created during the process of recycling batteries. “It contains recoverable quantities of critical minerals, including lithium, cobalt, nickel and manganese,” according to the government’s announcement of the ban, which argues the measure “will increase domestic recovery of lithium, cobalt, nickel and other critical minerals, thereby reducing import dependence and the associated foreign exchange outgo. It will also strengthen supply chains for battery manufacturing, electric vehicles, energy storage and clean-energy technologies.” “Further, the measure will advance the circular economy and ‘urban mining’, reducing reliance on primary mining, while supporting environmentally sound recycling of this hazardous material within the country in accordance with applicable environmental regulations.” Japanese giants to investigate orbiting datacenters Five giant Japanese companies – NTT, Mitsubishi Electric, MUFG Bank, the Development Bank of Japan, and telco NTT DOCOMO – last week signed a memorandum of understanding that will see them jointly explore development and operation of a mega-constellation of satellites. The five “will examine the technical and business feasibility of commercializing a diverse range of services enabled by mega-constellations, including communications, Earth observation, satellite-based positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT), and space data centers.” Mitsubishi already works with the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) to jointly develop and manufacture rockets. The two banks regularly back big infrastructure projects, while the two NTT entities have advanced comms expertise. The five companies didn’t set a deadline for delivery of a plan. If they do decide there’s a business opportunity, they’ll likely need to look beyond Japan for launch capacity as JAXA does not currently possess a re-usable launch vehicle and operates at a modest launch cadence compared to private launch operators. ®

item.title: Vulcan rocket fails during launch, dealing major blow to SpaceX competitors
item.description: United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket and 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites fell back to Earth minutes after liftoff Sunday, a crushing setback that will ripple across all sectors of the US space industry. The Vulcan rocket is on contract to launch roughly half of the US military's national security space missions in the next few years, and Sunday's mission was the first of 38 Vulcan launches booked by Amazon to build out its network of broadband Internet satellites aimed at competing with SpaceX's Starlink. Sunday's failure is expected to ground the rocket for an indefinite period of time. Vulcan is no stranger to close calls, having overcome failures with its strap-on solid rocket boosters on two of its four previous flights. In each case, the rocket corrected for those problems and continued into orbit to deploy its payloads. The incidents trigged months-long reviews and investigations before ULA could resume Vulcan flights. Read full article Comments

item.title: Diabetes: CAPPA urges FG, states to impose 20% sugary drinks tax, reform food policies
item.description: By Chioma Obinna On this day World Diabetes Day, the Corporate Accountability and Public Participation Africa (CAPPA) on Saturday called on the Federal Government and state governments to urgently reform Nigeria’s food policies, impose a minimum 20 per cent tax on sugar-sweetened beverages and tighten regulations on unhealthy food products to curb the rising burden of diabetes. The organisation warned that efforts to tackle the disease would yield limited results if government focused on screening and treatment while allowing aggressive marketing, widespread availability and affordability of ultra-processed foods and sugary drinks to continue unchecked. Making the call in a message to mark the 2026 World Diabetes Day, marked November 14, with the theme, “Early Action on Diabetes”, CAPPA said Nigeria faced an escalating diabetes crisis that required decisive government intervention beyond public awareness and individual lifestyle changes. According to the organisation, Nigeria has the highest number of adults aged 20 to 79 living with diabetes in Africa, while nearly three in four adults with diabetes across the continent remain undiagnosed. It warned that delayed diagnosis exposes millions of Nigerians to potentially life-threatening complications, including kidney failure, blindness, stroke and amputations. CAPPA also raised the alarm over the financial burden of diet-related non-communicable diseases, citing an estimated N1.92 trillion annual out-of-pocket expenditure by Nigerian households on their treatment. Executive Director of CAPPA, Akinbode Oluwafemi, said diabetes prevention should not be reduced to individual discipline when commercial interests and unhealthy food environments increasingly shape people’s dietary choices. He said: “We cannot keep telling Nigerians to eat healthily while allowing unhealthy food and beverages to dominate our markets, schools, advertisements and public spaces. “Early action on diabetes must begin with enacting and implementing strong regulatory policies that make healthy choices possible, affordable and accessible, not simply with advising people to change their dietary behaviour.” The organisation cited its 2025 report, Junk On Our Plates, which documented aggressive marketing of ultra-processed foods and beverages high in sugar and sodium across seven Nigerian states. It said the report exposed the targeting of children, young people and low-income communities through advertising, celebrity endorsements, misleading nutrition labels and cultural imagery designed to promote unhealthy products. To reverse the trend, CAPPA outlined five major policy interventions, beginning with the conclusion and enforcement of the proposed Sugar-Sweetened Beverage (SSB) tax. It urged the House of Representatives and the Federal Executive to complete legislative action following the Senate’s passage of the tax review bill earlier this year. The organisation advocated an inflation-adjusted excise tax of at least 20 per cent
item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: By Chioma Obinna On this day World Diabetes Day, the Corporate Accountability and Public Participation Africa (CAPPA) on Saturday called on the Federal Government and state governments to urgently reform Nigeria’s food policies, impose a minimum 20 per cent tax on sugar-sweetened beverages and tighten regulations on unhealthy food products to curb the rising burden of diabetes. The organisation warned that efforts to tackle the disease would yield limited results if government focused on screening and treatment while allowing aggressive marketing, widespread availability and affordability of ultra-processed foods and sugary drinks to continue unchecked. Making the call in a message to mark the 2026 World Diabetes Day, marked November 14, with the theme, “Early Action on Diabetes”, CAPPA said Nigeria faced an escalating diabetes crisis that required decisive government intervention beyond public awareness and individual lifestyle changes. According to the organisation, Nigeria has the highest number of adults aged 20 to 79 living with diabetes in Africa, while nearly three in four adults with diabetes across the continent remain undiagnosed. It warned that delayed diagnosis exposes millions of Nigerians to potentially life-threatening complications, including kidney failure, blindness, stroke and amputations. CAPPA also raised the alarm over the financial burden of diet-related non-communicable diseases, citing an estimated N1.92 trillion annual out-of-pocket expenditure by Nigerian households on their treatment. Executive Director of CAPPA, Akinbode Oluwafemi, said diabetes prevention should not be reduced to individual discipline when commercial interests and unhealthy food environments increasingly shape people’s dietary choices. He said: “We cannot keep telling Nigerians to eat healthily while allowing unhealthy food and beverages to dominate our markets, schools, advertisements and public spaces. “Early action on diabetes must begin with enacting and implementing strong regulatory policies that make healthy choices possible, affordable and accessible, not simply with advising people to change their dietary behaviour.” The organisation cited its 2025 report, Junk On Our Plates, which documented aggressive marketing of ultra-processed foods and beverages high in sugar and sodium across seven Nigerian states. It said the report exposed the targeting of children, young people and low-income communities through advertising, celebrity endorsements, misleading nutrition labels and cultural imagery designed to promote unhealthy products. To reverse the trend, CAPPA outlined five major policy interventions, beginning with the conclusion and enforcement of the proposed Sugar-Sweetened Beverage (SSB) tax. It urged the House of Representatives and the Federal Executive to complete legislative action following the Senate’s passage of the tax review bill earlier this year. The organisation advocated an inflation-adjusted excise tax of at least 20 per cent of the final retail price, in line with World Health Organisation recommendations. It further called for transparent utilisation of the revenue generated to fund diabetes prevention and control, primary healthcare, disease screening, subsidies for healthy local foods and nutrition programmes. CAPPA also urged the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) to introduce mandatory Front-of-Pack Warning Labels on packaged products containing excessive sugar, sodium and unhealthy fats. “Consumers have a fundamental right to know what is in their food without having to decode tiny, obscured print on the back of packages, as is currently the case,” it said. The organisation demanded statutory restrictions on the marketing and sponsorship of sugary drinks and ultra-processed foods targeting children and adolescents across television, digital platforms and public spaces. It also called on state governments to enforce federal public food procurement guidelines to ensure that schools, hospitals and other public institutions serve nutritious meals rather than ultra-processed products. On what it described as industry interference in nutrition policies, CAPPA cautioned against healthwashing by manufacturers, involving misleading health claims, selective fortification and lifestyle imagery to portray unhealthy products as nutritious. “Adding selected micronutrients to a sugary drink or a high-sodium bouillon cube does not erase excessive sugar, salt or other nutritional concerns. Fortification must never become a marketing licence to disguise unhealthy products or undermine policies that seek to reduce their consumption,” the organisation said. Beyond food regulation, CAPPA urged federal and state governments to increase funding for primary healthcare centres to provide free or subsidised blood glucose testing, essential medicines and improved access to insulin. It also advocated agricultural incentives for smallholder farmers producing indigenous fruits, vegetables and whole grains to improve the availability and affordability of nutritious local foods. Oluwafemi said: “Diabetes is not inevitable, and early action against the condition must include action against the commercial practices that make unhealthy diets increasingly difficult to avoid. “On this World Diabetes Day, we call on Nigerian lawmakers and regulators to choose the health and productivity of our people over the profit margins of ultra-processed food corporations.” The post Diabetes: CAPPA urges FG, states to impose 20% sugary drinks tax, reform food policies appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Hopkins’ late stunner sends Kansas City past Gotham and into NWSL final
item.description: Hopkins’ 89th-minute volley seals dramatic 2-1 upset Bethune scores stunning free kick against top seeds Current to face Washington Spirit for first NWSL title After a week dominated by a headline-grabbing stadium imbroglio , Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current finally got down to the vital business of their NWSL semi-final on Sunday afternoon, a frigid encounter at an unlikely venue on New York City’s Randall’s Island with a place in next Saturday’s championship match at stake. Haley Hopkins delivered the knockout blow at the death, hitting an 89th-minute volley off the crossbar and in to seal a 2-1 upset that left Gotham FC’s title defense in tatters. Paired with Croix Bethune’s first-half free-kick stunner, the late winner sent fourth-seeded Kansas City past the defending champions into a championship showdown in six days against the Washington Spirit. item.title: England End Spain’s 44-Game Unbeaten Run With Nations League Win
item.description: England snapped world champions Spain’s unbeaten run with a 3-2 victory in Madrid on Sunday to clinch the top spot in Nations League group A3. Goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White inflicted La Roja’s first loss in a competitive game since March 2023, after 44 without defeat. England’s Elliot Anderson was sent off in the second half as Spain fought back from three goals down with strikes from Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams, but Luis de la Fuente’s World Cup winners could not find the equaliser. Both sides were already sure to progress, but as group winners England will be seeded for the quarter-finals in March. England coach Thomas Tuchel selected James Trafford in goal over Jordan Pickford and also brought White and Konsa into the side. Teenage star Lamine Yamal was fit to start for Spain at Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano stadium after missing their midweek win over the Czech Republic. However the youngster did not see much of the ball in the first half as England came out strongly. Spain’s midfielder #09 Fermin Lopez challenges England’s goalkeeper #13 James Trafford during the UEFA Nations League – League A day 6 group 3 – football match between Spain and England at Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid on November 15, 2026. (Photo by Thomas COEX / AFP) Spain goalkeeper Unai Simon produced a strong reaction save to deny Jude Bellingham, while Anthony Gordon had a dangerous shot blocked. Ballon d’Or winner Kane, who beat Yamal to the award, sent an effort narrowly wide. Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsi handed England the advantage when he clumsily felled Kane in the area on the stroke of half time. The Bayern Munich hitman powered a perfect penalty past Simon, who dived the right way but to no avail. De la Fuente tried to react at half-time with a triple change, including throwing on Barcelona duo Fermin Lopez and Pedri, but England quickly found more joy. England’s midfielder #17 Morgan Rogers fights for the ball with Spain’s forward #17 Nico Williams during the UEFA Nations League – League A day 6 group 3 – football match between Spain and England at Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid on November 15, 2026. (Photo by Javier SORIANO / AFP) Konsa headed home the second from Declan Rice’s corner in the 53rd minute after the Arsenal defender was left unmarked by Spain’s defence. Four minutes later England sliced open Spain’s defence with Kane and Bellingham combining to set up White for the third. La Roja clawed their way back into the game when Elliot Anderson fouled Yamal in the area as the Spain striker ran in on goal. The Manchester City midfielder was dismissed and Mikel Oyarzabal slotted home the penalty. Spain found a second when Gordon gave the ball away and Yamal fed Nico Williams, whose shot hit the post and bounced in. Williams curled over and Trafford denied Yamal and Marc Cucurella as Spain looked fruitlessly for the goal they needed to preserve their unbeaten record. item.title: England end Spain’s 44-game unbeaten run with 3-2 win
item.description: England snapped world champions Spain’s record unbeaten run with a 3-2 victory in Madrid on Sunday to clinch the top spot in Nations League group A3. Goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White inflicted La Roja’s first loss in a competitive game since March 2023, after 44 without defeat. England’s Elliot Anderson was sent off in the second half as Spain fought back from three goals down with strikes from Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams, but Luis de la Fuente’s World Cup winners could not find the equaliser. Both sides were already sure to progress, but as group winners England will be seeded for the quarter-finals in March. Spain had beaten England in the Euro 2024 final before adding a second world crown this summer, while the Three Lions finished third. “We knew we were going to beat them tonight, the message from the manager after the Croatia game (on Thursday) has been so positive,” England midfielder Declan Rice told ITV. “The first 10 minutes was the best we’ve played.” England coach Thomas Tuchel hailed his team on their superb performance in the Spanish capital. “We brought everything to the table,” Tuchel told ITV. “We were brave. Spirit wise, energy wise and also football quality was (all at the) highest level.” Tuchel selected James Trafford in goal over Jordan Pickford and also brought White and Konsa into the side. Teenage star Lamine Yamal was fit to start for Spain at Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano stadium after missing their midweek win over the Czech Republic. However the youngster did not see much of the ball in the first half as England came out strongly. Spain goalkeeper Unai Simon produced a strong reaction save to deny Jude Bellingham, while Anthony Gordon had a dangerous shot blocked. Ballon d’Or winner Kane, who beat Yamal to the award, sent an effort narrowly wide. Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsi handed England the advantage when he clumsily felled Kane in the area on the stroke of half time. The Bayern Munich hitman powered a perfect penalty past Simon, who dived the right way but to no avail. – Quickfire double – De la Fuente tried to react at half-time with a triple change, including throwing on Barcelona duo Fermin Lopez and Pedri, but England quickly found more joy. Konsa headed home the second from Declan Rice’s corner in the 53rd minute after the Arsenal defender was left unmarked by Spain’s defence. Four minutes later England sliced open Spain’s defence with Kane and Bellingham combining to set up White for the third. Including friendlies, Spain had gone 43 straight matches without defeat. “On the pitch everything happens very fast, it’s a pity,” Oyarzabal told TVE about England’s two goals early in the second half. “You have to focus on what came after, the reaction — the team never stopped pushing, never stopped trying… their goalkeeper also deserves credit for us not having equalised.” The post England end Spain’s 44-game unbeaten run with 3-2 win appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: England fend off fiery Spain fightback after Anderson’s red to top Nations League group
item.description: It was the game to show Thomas Tuchel where his rebooted England team had got to; surely the ultimate test in international football. Spain in Spain. A world champion team who, in Tuchel’s words, had “forgotten how to lose.” Before this Nations League group decider, they had been beaten only once in 43 matches – on penalties against Portugal in the final of this competition last year. What England produced for 65 minutes was extraordinary. What followed was equally so for different reasons. When it was over, England had made the most sensational of statements. Back in 2018, on their previous visit to Spain, England won 3-2 in Seville in the Nations League; it was one of Sir Gareth Southgate’s most famous results, an ignition point. It was the same scoreline and the same feeling for Tuchel on Sunday night. Continue reading...

item.title: 2027: Soludo urges politicians to keep off places of worship
item.description: Gov. Chukwuma Soludo of Anambra has urged politicians to keep politics away from places of worship, saying religious institutions should remain centres of spiritual growth and unity. Soludo made the call during a visit to the Mountain of Holy Ghost Intervention Deliverance Ministry Inc., Onitsha, to celebrate its 30th anniversary. The ministry was founded by Prophet Chukwuemeka Ohanaemere, popularly known as Odumeje. He said: “Politicians, keep off places of worship! I do not do politics in the house of God. “I deliberately avoided church campaigns for six months before the last governorship election in Anambra. “My visit to religious institutions is usually motivated by my commitment to ecumenism and responsibility as the father of all in the state”. The governor described the anniversary as a significant milestone, noting that it marked maturity, preparation and a new phase in the ministry’s growth. He recalled that his first encounter with the ministry was during the demolition of part of its structure by the state government to facilitate the dredging of the Sakamori drainage channel. Soludo commended Odumeje for his contributions to charity and efforts towards societal development. He also acknowledged the cleric’s support for the state’s campaign against criminal idolatry and activities of illegal traditional spiritual practitioners. According to him, the advocacy, alongside the Anambra Homeland Security Law, has contributed to making the state safer. Responding, Odumeje pledged continued partnership with the state government to drive progress and development. The post 2027: Soludo urges politicians to keep off places of worship appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Disu assures Abia residents of improved security
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The Inspector-General of Police (IGP), Olatunji Disu, has assured residents of Abia State of improved security, pledging that the Nigeria Police Force would intensify efforts to protect lives and property across the state. Disu gave the assurance during a courtesy visit to Governor Alex Otti at Government House, Umuahia, where he commended the governor for his sustained support to the police. The IGP, who said he had received positive reports from the Commissioner of Police and the Assistant Inspector-General of Police on the state government’s assistance to the Force, promised that the police would reciprocate the gesture through improved service delivery. “I want to thank you for all you have been doing for my officers. My Commissioner of Police has told me all you have been doing for us. The AIG too reiterated it. Thank you so much for it,” Disu said. He assured the governor that the police would remain committed to tackling security challenges and ensuring the safety of residents. “I will give you my word that we will continue to do our best to ensure proper policing so that people of the state will be able to sleep with their two eyes closed,” he said. Disu explained that his visit to Abia was primarily to attend the traditional marriage ceremony of his orderly, Victor Nnah Sunday, at Amangwu, Abaki-Ndoki, in Ukwa East Local Government Area. He, however, said he considered it necessary to pay homage to Otti, as the state’s Chief Security Officer, before proceeding to the wedding venue. Responding, Otti commended the police leadership for its professionalism and prompt response to the state government’s requests for assistance in addressing security challenges. “Thank you for what you do for the country. Thank you for the professionalism of the Force and for making everyone realise that the safety and security of the people is paramount. “We have had instances where we called upon you and you responded swiftly,” the governor said. Otti also praised the promotion of the immediate past Commissioner of Police in Abia to the rank of Assistant Inspector-General of Police, describing his service in the state as professional and tactful. He said the former police commissioner demonstrated commitment in handling security matters, adding that although the state would have preferred to retain him, his elevation was a welcome development. “He demonstrated professionalism and tact in the discharge of his duties. If not that it is a promotion, we would have resisted it, but we believe it is good for him to move on,” Otti said. The governor expressed optimism that the officer would sustain his relationship with Abia despite his new position. Otti also congratulated the IGP’s orderly on his traditional marriage, recalling that he had met him during an earlier encounter with the police chief. My Commissioner of Police has told me all you have been doing for us. The AIG too reiterated it. Thank you so much for it,” Disu said. He assured the governor that the police would remain committed to tackling security challenges and ensuring the safety of residents. “I will give you my word that we will continue to do our best to ensure proper policing so that people of the state will be able to sleep with their two eyes closed,” he said. Disu explained that his visit to Abia was primarily to attend the traditional marriage ceremony of his orderly, Victor Nnah Sunday, at Amangwu, Abaki-Ndoki, in Ukwa East Local Government Area. He, however, said he considered it necessary to pay homage to Otti, as the state’s Chief Security Officer, before proceeding to the wedding venue. Responding, Otti commended the police leadership for its professionalism and prompt response to the state government’s requests for assistance in addressing security challenges. “Thank you for what you do for the country. Thank you for the professionalism of the Force and for making everyone realise that the safety and security of the people is paramount. “We have had instances where we called upon you and you responded swiftly,” the governor said. Otti also praised the promotion of the immediate past Commissioner of Police in Abia to the rank of Assistant Inspector-General of Police, describing his service in the state as professional and tactful. He said the former police commissioner demonstrated commitment in handling security matters, adding that although the state would have preferred to retain him, his elevation was a welcome development. “He demonstrated professionalism and tact in the discharge of his duties. If not that it is a promotion, we would have resisted it, but we believe it is good for him to move on,” Otti said. The governor expressed optimism that the officer would sustain his relationship with Abia despite his new position. Otti also congratulated the IGP’s orderly on his traditional marriage, recalling that he had met him during an earlier encounter with the police chief. The governor further commended Disu for what he described as his demonstration of national inclusiveness through the choice of aides and associates from different ethnic and geographical backgrounds. He specifically noted that some of the IGP’s close aides hailed from different parts of the country, including Ohafia in Abia State. Otti urged Nigerians to rise above ethnic and geographical sentiments, stressing that national unity would be strengthened when citizens saw themselves first as members of one country. The IGP was accompanied on the visit by his wife, AIG Afolabi and some Commissioners of Police. Members of the governor’s delegation included the Chief of Staff, Pastor Caleb Ajagba; Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu; Commissioner for Arts, Culture and Creative Economy, Dr Matthew Ekwuribe; and other top government officials. item.title: 2027: Atiku promises to end insecurity if elected
item.description: By Nabilu Balarabe The Presidential candidate of African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar has promised to tackle insurgency and other forms of insecurity, if voted in the 2027 Presidential election. Atiku made the promise in Potiskum on Sunday during the party’s campaign rally. He also promised to provide an enabling environment for youths to develop careers in all areas of their interest. “Whatever you want to do, my administration will support you. But we will not allow all acts of violence,” he said. Abubakar said he would revive the economy by providing affordable fuel, electricity and cutting taxes. He, however, said all these could only be achieved if voters came out en-mass to vote for him in the forthcoming election. Abubakar advised the electorate to vote wisely for candidates that would better their lot and reject corrupt and selfish politicians. “Vote the ADC for your future and the future of your children. We are ready to serve you in every way we can,” Atiku said. In his remarks, the ADC National Secretary, Mr Rauf Aregbesola, thanked the people of Yobe for their warm reception to the party’s candidates. He urged the electorate to vote for change and ensure that due process was followed in counting and collation of votes cast. The post 2027: Atiku promises to end insecurity if elected appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Wizkid, Jada P celebrates daughter Morayo’s 2nd birthday
item.description: Nigerian music star, Ayodeji Balogun, popularly known as Wizkid, and his partner, Jada P, have celebrated the second birthday of their daughter, Morayo. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that Jada P shared adorable photographs of their two-year-old, with balloons and a beautifully decorated birthday cake on her X page (formally Twitter) @jada3_p on Sunday. Post reads: “My Daughter is TWO”. The birthday post attracted warm wishes from fans who flooded social media with congratulatory messages and videos celebrating Morayo, fondly called “Big Mo” and “Princess Morayo.” Some fans also linked the birthday date to Wizkid’s 2024 single, “Kese (Dance),” from his album dedicated to his late mother. The family has also made public appearances together, including at the opening of Kōzo in Los Angeles, where they were seen sharing smiles marking the milestone with a celebration of the toddler’s growth. The post Wizkid, Jada P celebrates daughter Morayo’s 2nd birthday appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: One firefighter injured as hoodlums attack crew in Abuja
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — One firefighter was injured after suspected hoodlums attacked a Federal Fire Service crew responding to a fire emergency at 7th Avenue, Gwarinpa, Abuja, at the weekend. The suspected perpetrators have reportedly been arrested and are under investigation following the incident. The Federal Capital Territory Command of the service condemned the attack in a statement issued by its Public Relations Officer, Superintendent of Fire Anyam Barnabas. The statement said the firefighters, attached to the Kubwa Metropolitan Fire Station, were responding to a distress call from a resident, Mrs Amina, at about 10am when they came under attack. On arrival at the scene, the crew were reportedly pelted with stones by suspected hoodlums, leaving one firefighter injured. The injured officer was immediately taken to a hospital for medical attention. The incident was reported to the Galadima Police Station, while the suspects were said to be under investigation. The Controller of the Federal Fire Service, FCT Command, Mohammed Anas, expressed displeasure over what he described as persistent attacks on firefighters while carrying out their statutory responsibilities. He warned that anyone who attacked or obstructed firefighters at emergency scenes would face the consequences of the law. Anas urged residents of the FCT to appreciate and support firefighters, particularly during emergency operations, and called on those involved in such acts to desist. He reaffirmed the command’s commitment to prompt and effective emergency response across the territory, stressing that firefighters must be allowed to perform their duties without intimidation, harassment or attacks. The controller also appealed to residents to cooperate with emergency responders and provide the necessary support to enable them to save lives and protect property. The post One firefighter injured as hoodlums attack crew in Abuja appeared first on Vanguard News .
